# Measurement scope

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 3, 5, 6 · Agent: read-only

Defines what test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size mean, so that figures from different runs compare. Record every figure in `run-log.json` → `codeMetrics` and in `docs/06_verification-report.md` with its scope, level and tool. The project selects paths and exclusions in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Mutation scope"); this file never names them.

## Constraints

- Do not change a tool's scope, filters, exclusions or thresholds to improve a number. A change is a decision record.
- Do not report a figure without its scope, level and tool.
- Production code is the source a component ships. It excludes tests, generated code, the application entry point and anything listed under "Measurement exclusions" in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with a reason. Decide the exclusions in phase 3, before any test is written; do not extend them later.
- Test code never counts towards coverage or mutation.

## Test counts

Per component and level (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e`), passed and failed, from the runner's own report.

## Coverage

Line and branch, per component, as three figures: `unit` (unit tests only), `nonUnit` (integration, acceptance and end-to-end tests that exercise the component) and `all` (one merged report). The headline figure is `all`.

## Mutation score

- **Scope:** all production code of the component, narrowed only to the paths in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` "Mutation scope", which are the same in every run of the project (default: all production code). Do not narrow it by running only some tests or by excluding packages that are not listed there.
- **Tests:** the component's full automated suite, at every level it has, so the score does not depend on which level the agent ran. If that is infeasible, record the tests actually run and the reason in a decision record.
- **Record:** `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`. `score` (raw) = killed (timed-out counts as killed) ÷ all mutants the tool generated; a mutant no test reaches counts as survived. `scoreAdjusted` = (killed + equivalent) ÷ total, where `equivalent` is the number of survivors justified as equivalent. `scoreCovered` = killed ÷ mutants a test reaches.
- Do not remove equivalent mutants by hand. List every survivor you count as equivalent in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with the class and method, the mutation and the reason it cannot change behaviour; a survivor without that entry is not equivalent. Always record the raw score next to the adjusted score.

## Code size

`cloc` (same version in every run): production = non-test source and resources, test = test sources including end-to-end tests. Generated code and lock files are excluded.

## Mutation run discipline

- Measure coverage and mutation score in phase 5, so that surviving mutants are handled before verification. Phase 6 repeats a measurement only for a component whose code or tests changed since, and only once, after the last fix.
- Do not start a full mutation run on code that is not final. One full run per component per measurement; the only other runs are the targeted survivor rounds and the one confirming full run after the last round of the quality gate (below).
- Check once, before the full run, that the tool works: a mutant in code the tests plainly cover must be killed. A score far below the line coverage (for example 25 % at 100 % coverage) means the tool is not activating mutants (known case: Stryker with the wrong Vitest major version); stop and raise a decision, do not record the figure.
- Start a long run in the background and continue with other checks of the phase; read its log only for the summary lines. Do not hold the session in a blocking wait on it.

## Quality gate

The gate is the same in every run of the project: the thresholds in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Thresholds"), per component, over the scope and with the tests defined above. It makes runs comparable: every run reaches the same quality, and what differs is the cost of reaching it.

- **Gate:** line coverage (`all`) at or above the line threshold, and `scoreAdjusted` at or above the mutation threshold. Branch coverage is recorded only.
- **Order in phase 5:** write the unit and integration tests area by area and measure line coverage after each area (fast) until the line threshold is met; then run mutation testing **once** per component (full run); then, if `scoreAdjusted` is below the threshold, up to **three** survivor rounds: each adds tests aimed at the survivors in the code that matters most (validation, security, persistence, business rules first) and re-runs only the mutated classes, with one confirming full run after the last round.
- **Stop at the gate:** once a component meets both thresholds, add no further test and start no further mutation run for it. Do not add tests for coverage or score beyond the gate.
- **Shortfall:** after the third round a component still below a threshold is recorded as a shortfall (which threshold, by how many points) in a non-blocking decision and as a finding, and the run continues. Do not change the scope, the tests run or the exclusions to reach a threshold; that is a decision record at most.
- **Record in `run-log.json`:** `codeMetrics.gate` = `{ thresholds: {lineCoverage, mutationScore}, perComponent: { <name>: { lineMet, mutationMet, lineShortfall, mutationShortfall } }, mutationRounds: { <name>: n }, testsAtFirstMutation: { <name>: n }, met: true|false }`; `mutationRounds` is 0 when the first full run already met the gate.

# Severity scale

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 0, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

The only levels used anywhere. Critical and High block release.

| Level | Definition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Exploitable now, or total loss of a core user story with no workaround | Unauthenticated access to protected data; accepted input that is silently not stored |
| High | Exploitable under realistic conditions, or a core user story degraded for a plausible group of users | Missing authorization check on one operation; a limit that locks out legitimate users |
| Medium | A real defect with limited impact, or a control weaker than required | A dependency vulnerability with no reachable exploit path; a duplicated validation rule |
| Low | Cosmetic, stylistic, or a theoretical or false-positive finding | A lint warning; a scanner match on constant input |

## Rules

- Tools that report Critical/High/Medium/Low (or CVSS) are used as reported.
- Lowering a Critical or High to Medium or Low needs written evidence (e.g. the vulnerable feature is not used) and is a blocking decision.
- A surviving mutant in security-, validation- or persistence-related code is classified individually.

## Tool mapping

Extend when a project adds a tool with its own scale.

| Tool type | Tool's level | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| CVSS-based (dependency scanners) | 9.0–10.0 / 7.0–8.9 / 4.0–6.9 / 0.1–3.9 | Critical / High / Medium / Low |
| Rule-based SAST with ERROR/WARNING/INFO | ERROR / WARNING / INFO | High / Medium / Low |
| Rank or priority 1–5 scales | 1 / 2 / 3–5 | High / Medium / Low |
| Bug-rank 1–20 scales | 1–4 / 5–9 / 10–20 | High / Medium / Low |

# Test strategy

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: every phase that writes or runs tests · Agent: read-only

When each test level is written and whether it is frozen is defined in `general/phases.md`. Project thresholds are in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.

## Constraints

- Do not test acceptance behaviour through internals; use the component's public interface (API, UI, CLI, messages).
- Do not depend on live external services in automated tests; use the local substitutes in `project/00_setup/environments.md` and list the real services in the release notes for manual testing.
- Do not leave flaky, skipped or disabled tests; fix them or record a decision.
- Do not weaken an assertion to make an incorrect implementation pass.
- Test names contain the AC id they verify.

## First complete run

Record the result of the first full run before fixing anything, then classify each failure:

| Class | Action |
|---|---|
| Implementation defect | fix the code |
| Defect in a non-frozen test | fix the test and say so in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` |
| Frozen test appears wrong | blocking decision; do not touch the test |

## Measures (recorded in every project)

Test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: what each covers, at which level and with which tool.

## Manifest

name: write-acceptance-tests
description: Write and freeze the black-box acceptance tests from the given acceptance criteria and end-to-end scenarios and the contracts, before any production code exists (phase 3).

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phase 3 · Agent: read-only

- Reads: `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/01_requirements/e2e-scenarios.md`, `docs/02_contracts/`, `general/quality/test-strategy.md`, `general/phases.md`
- Writes: acceptance and end-to-end tests, `docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256`, `docs/03_test-strategy.md`
- Does not read: production source code

## Procedure

1. For every AC, write at least one test through the component's public interface that checks the observable outcome the AC states. For a rejection AC, also check that nothing changed. For every scenario in `e2e-scenarios.md`, write exactly one end-to-end test; write no other end-to-end test, and do not split or merge scenarios.
2. Put the AC id in each test name.
3. Run the suite. Every test must fail because the behaviour is missing, not because of a build, configuration or harness error; a test that passes only on bootstrap code is listed in step 4. Fix the harness until that holds.
4. Record the run (pass/fail counts and a one-line reason per group of failures) in `docs/03_test-strategy.md`.
5. Self-check every assertion and helper before the freeze, because a defective frozen test costs a blocking decision: confirm that a correct implementation can make it pass, and that it cannot pass or fail for the wrong reason. Check what each helper returns and what each matcher compares (known cases: the PostgreSQL JDBC driver returns java.sql.Timestamp, not OffsetDateTime, for 	imestamptz unless the type is requested; AssertJ doesNotContain on a  yte[] tests single bytes, not a byte sequence, so compare the first bytes with Arrays.copyOf instead). A test must not contradict another assertion in the same test.
6. Format and lint the tests now; after freezing they cannot change.
7. Commit the tests story by story as you finish them. Then write the manifest (normalised line endings) and commit it alone as the freeze commit.

4. Start every component as described for its target environment and exercise the core user flows at runtime; record what was run and what was observed.

- **Stop at the gate:** once a component meets both thresholds, add no further test and start no further mutation run for it. Do not add tests for coverage or score beyond the gate.
- **Shortfall:** after the third round a component still below a threshold is recorded as a shortfall (which threshold, by how many points) in a non-blocking decision and as a finding, and the run continues. Do not change the scope, the tests run or the exclusions to reach a threshold; that is a decision record at most.
- **Record in `run-log.json`:** `codeMetrics.gate` = `{ thresholds: {lineCoverage, mutationScore}, perComponent: { <name>: { lineMet, mutationMet, lineShortfall, mutationShortfall } }, mutationRounds: { <name>: n }, testsAtFirstMutation: { <name>: n }, met: true|false }`; `mutationRounds` is 0 when the first full run already met the gate.

# Severity scale

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 0, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

The only levels used anywhere. Critical and High block release.

| Level | Definition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Exploitable now, or total loss of a core user story with no workaround | Unauthenticated access to protected data; accepted input that is silently not stored |
| High | Exploitable under realistic conditions, or a core user story degraded for a plausible group of users | Missing authorization check on one operation; a limit that locks out legitimate users |
| Medium | A real defect with limited impact, or a control weaker than required | A dependency vulnerability with no reachable exploit path; a duplicated validation rule |
| Low | Cosmetic, stylistic, or a theoretical or false-positive finding | A lint warning; a scanner match on constant input |

## Rules

- Tools that report Critical/High/Medium/Low (or CVSS) are used as reported.
- Lowering a Critical or High to Medium or Low needs written evidence (e.g. the vulnerable feature is not used) and is a blocking decision.
- A surviving mutant in security-, validation- or persistence-related code is classified individually.

## Tool mapping

Extend when a project adds a tool with its own scale.

| Tool type | Tool's level | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| CVSS-based (dependency scanners) | 9.0–10.0 / 7.0–8.9 / 4.0–6.9 / 0.1–3.9 | Critical / High / Medium / Low |
| Rule-based SAST with ERROR/WARNING/INFO | ERROR / WARNING / INFO | High / Medium / Low |
| Rank or priority 1–5 scales | 1 / 2 / 3–5 | High / Medium / Low |
| Bug-rank 1–20 scales | 1–4 / 5–9 / 10–20 | High / Medium / Low |

# Test strategy

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: every phase that writes or runs tests · Agent: read-only

When each test level is written and whether it is frozen is defined in `general/phases.md`. Project thresholds are in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.

## Constraints

- Do not test acceptance behaviour through internals; use the component's public interface (API, UI, CLI, messages).
- Do not depend on live external services in automated tests; use the local substitutes in `project/00_setup/environments.md` and list the real services in the release notes for manual testing.
- Do not leave flaky, skipped or disabled tests; fix them or record a decision.
- Do not weaken an assertion to make an incorrect implementation pass.
- Test names contain the AC id they verify.

## First complete run

Record the result of the first full run before fixing anything, then classify each failure:

| Class | Action |
|---|---|
| Implementation defect | fix the code |
| Defect in a non-frozen test | fix the test and say so in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` |
| Frozen test appears wrong | blocking decision; do not touch the test |

## Measures (recorded in every project)

Test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: what each covers, at which level and with which tool.

`docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256` uses `sha256sum` format with paths relative to `02_output/`, hashed after LF normalisation.

# Metrics

> Owner: Experiment lead · Read in: every phase and post-run · Agent: read-only

Experiment measurement only. Record observed values; never estimate. An unobservable value stays `null` with a `<field>Reason`.

Goal column: **↓** lower is better, **↑** higher is better, **=** should equal the stated value, **i** information for interpreting other numbers.

## Principles

- **Human waiting is not part of the result.** Agent time is wall time minus every wait for a human. A wait over one hour also lets the 1-hour prompt cache expire, and the call after it writes the whole context again; that rebuild is a cost of the wait, so `usage.costUsdExclWaits` removes it. Compare runs on agent time and `costUsdExclWaits`.
- **Record only what only you can see, and with the clock tool.** The agent records what happened (waits, loops, decisions, deviations, test and quality results). Timestamps come from `tools/stat.mjs`, never from memory or estimates. Everything that can be computed from the transcripts and git is computed after the run by `tools/build-report.mjs`, so the run spends no calls on it.
- **Make runs comparable.** Say what a number covers. Scope, level and tool of coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

## 1. Agent, during the run → `run-log.json`

Phase 0, first action: `node 03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs init`. It creates `run-log.json` from the template, a unique `runId`, the start time and commit, the transcript path and the environment. It prints what it wrote.

| Field | When | How | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId`, `model`, `effort`, `templateVersion`, `start`, `startCommit`, `transcript`, `environment` | phase 0 | written by `stat.mjs init` from `run-config.md`, git and the host | i |
| `phases[].start`, `phases[].end` | every phase boundary | `stat.mjs phase <n> start` and `stat.mjs phase <n> end`; a start also closes the previous phase, `phase 7 end` also sets `end` and `finalCommit` | ↓ agent time per phase |
| `humanInterventions[]` | every time the agent waits for the human or the human acts, including stops, restarts and installs | `stat.mjs wait start <cause> "<reason>" [decisionId]` when you ask or stop, `stat.mjs wait end` when work resumes. `cause`: `decision`, `environment`, `approval`, `session`, `other` | ↓ count and minutes; every minute here is excluded from agent time |
| `firstTestRun`, `finalTestRun` | first full run before fixes; last full run | edit the file: `passed`, `failed` and `byLevel` (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e` counts) | first: ↓ failed (defects the first run found); final: ↑ passed, `failed` = 0 |
| `acceptanceCriteria` | end of phase 3; changes in phase 4 | `total` criteria, `frozenTests`, `frozenTestChanges[]` as `{decisionId, reason}` | ↑ criteria covered by tests; ↓ frozen-test changes (each one needed a human) |
| `findings` | end of phase 6 | counts by severity, as found | ↓ |
| `openAtEnd` | end of phase 6 | Critical, High and Medium findings still open after triage | = 0 for Critical and High |
| `fixLoops[]` | each verify → fix → re-verify loop | `{loop, findings, category, needsHuman, change, start, end}`. `category`: `test-gap`, `security-config`, `dependency`, `defect`, `process`, `tooling`. `start` is the first fix action, `end` the clean re-check (UTC, `date -u +%FT%TZ`) | ↓ minutes per loop; a loop that repeats across runs belongs in the template |
| `decisions[]` | each decision record | `{id, type, phase, category, start, end}`; `type` `blocking` or `non-blocking`; `category`: `environment`, `dependency`, `security-finding`, `frozen-test`, `requirement`, `other`; `end` = when resolved | ↓ blocking; a category that repeats across runs can be answered in advance |
| `divergences[]` | whenever the run departs from `AGENTS.md`, `working-rules.md`, `phases.md` or the stack | `{phase, ref, divergence}`; includes steps done without the required question, scope reduced, versions replaced | = 0; each one makes the run less comparable |
| `codeMetrics` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 for a changed component | per component: `productionLoc`, `testLoc`, `lineCoverage` and `branchCoverage` as `{unit, nonUnit, all}`, `mutation` as `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`, plus complexity and duplication; scope, level and counting as in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` | ↑ coverage and mutation score (always with scope); = 0 duplication |
| `codeMetrics.gate` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 | the quality gate of `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: `thresholds`, `perComponent` (`lineMet`, `mutationMet`, shortfalls in points), `mutationRounds` and `testsAtFirstMutation` per component, `met` | `met` true; few rounds |

`commits[]` and `commitSummary` are not recorded by the agent: the post-run step reads them from `git log`.

## 2. Post-run session → `run-log.json`, `results/`, `data/`

Started after the run ends, in a new session whose only task is: "Run `node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics` and report what it prints. Do not change anything else." Before it, run `/cost` once in the finished session (the plan limits are then captured in the transcript). The script:

1. measures the run from the session transcript(s), the sub-agent transcripts next to them and `git log`, and stores `time`, `usage`, `environment`, `commits`, `commitSummary` in `run-log.json`;
2. copies the transcripts to `03_statistics/data/` (committed with the run, so the measuring can be repeated on any machine; the recorded path is used when it exists, the copy otherwise);
3. writes everything it generates to `03_statistics/results/`: `run-report.html` (every attribute with goal, direction and value), `measurements.json`, `usage-panel.md`, `commits.csv`, `transcript.md` (readable session, needs Python 3);
4. fills the empty cells of the panel table in `usage.md` from the harness's own accounting (the `cost-state` record in the transcript).

Options: `--no-write` leaves `run-log.json` and `usage.md` alone, `--no-md` skips `transcript.md`, `--no-backup` skips `data/`. If `transcript` is missing from `run-log.json`, find the session with `py 03_statistics/tools/claude_chat_to_md.py --list`, put the path of its `.jsonl` in `transcript` (a resumed run lists every session file in `transcripts`) and run the script again. Without any transcript the report still builds from phases and recorded waits; cost, tokens, model and tool time, context and cache rebuilds are then not recorded.

| Field | What it is | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| `time.agentMin` | sum over phases of wall time minus waits (recorded interventions and idle gaps above 10 minutes in the transcript) | ↓ |
| `time.humanWaitMin`, `time.waitsOver60Min`, `time.longWaits[]` | excluded waiting, and each wait over an hour with its cause | ↓; = 0 waits over an hour |
| `time.modelMin`, `time.toolMin` | transcript time spent generating and running tools | ↓; tool time shows what to automate or speed up |
| `time.unrecordedIdleMin` | idle time in the transcript that `humanInterventions` does not cover | = 0 (a recording gap) |
| `time.phaseChecks` | phase boundaries written by `stat.mjs` against typed ones, and implausible timestamps | all via `stat.mjs`, no issues |
| `time.byPhase[]` | wall, wait, agent, model and tool minutes per phase | ↓ in phases 0, 1, 2, 7 (overhead); phases 4 to 6 hold the real work |
| `usage.inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `thinkingTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `modelCalls` | sums over every model call, each call counted once, sub-agents included | ↓ |
| `usage.toolCalls` | total, errors, per tool name | ↓ calls and errors |
| `usage.costUsd` | tokens × the prices in `usage.md`, per model | ↓ |
| `usage.costUsdExclWaits` | `costUsd` minus the cache rebuilds that followed a wait over an hour | ↓ (the comparison figure) |
| `usage.cacheRebuilds[]` | each cache write above 150k tokens, the wait before it and its extra cost | = none caused by waits |
| `usage.subagents` | sub-agent calls, transcripts found, their cost (inside `costUsd`) | i; a call without a transcript is a measuring gap |
| `usage.panel`, `usage.check` | the harness's own totals (`cost-state`) and the difference to our calculation | difference within 1.5 % |
| `usage.byPhase[]` | calls, tokens, cost and average context per phase | ↓ in late phases, where context is largest |
| `usage.context` | peak and average context tokens per call, share of calls above 150k | ↓ (every call re-reads the whole context) |
| `usage.toolTimeByCategory` | minutes and calls per command class (backend build, mutation, e2e, …) | ↓ for the largest classes |
| `commits[]` | per commit: phase, type, files, changed lines (without logs, lock files, generated folders), concerns touched, size and message checks, minutes since the previous commit (waits removed), model calls and cost since the previous commit | commits small and finished: ≤ 15 files and ≤ 400 lines, one concern, `<type>: <summary> (IDs)` |
| `commitSummary` | counts, median and maximum size, shares over the size guide, mixed, with a correct message, in a burst (within a minute of the previous), cost and minutes between commits, cost per 100 lines | ↓ oversize, mixed and burst; ↑ correct messages |
| `environment` | operator, machine, plan, permission mode (from `run-config.md`), the host the run started on (account, CPU, memory, working directory; read by `stat.mjs init`), operating system and tool versions (at the start), harness version, entry point, models, effort and permission modes seen (from the transcripts), measuring host | i; needed to explain differences between runs |

## 3. Human → `usage.md`

Prices before the post-run session (one row per model id, shape as in the file). After it only `Approval prompts` is yours; the other cells are filled automatically when empty, and anything you wrote stays. A mismatch between the harness's total and our calculation is reported in the last row.

# Run guide

This setup is run three times, once each by kyuhi, tanej and tjan, in one shared environment, and the three runs are compared. Everything below is therefore the same for everyone; the only things that may differ are the four lines in the table "If you are not kyuhi".

## 1. Prepare the run folder
1. **Copy the template** (the folder `kyuhi_single-agent_sdd_v006_structure`) to a new folder named after the run, for example `kyuhi_single-agent_sdd_v006`. Open a terminal in it.
2. **Initialise git on the run's branch and keep `.env` out of git before you create it.** The branch is named `<operator>/single-agent/sdd/v006` (for kyuhi: `kyuhi/single-agent/sdd/v006`).
   - `git init -b kyuhi/single-agent/sdd/v006` (use your own operator name)
   - then exclude `.env` (the template has no `.gitignore`; the agent writes one in phase 0):
   - Git Bash: `echo .env >> .git/info/exclude`
   - PowerShell: `Add-Content -Encoding ascii .git\info\exclude ".env"`
3. **Copy the project inputs** `01_input/01_project/` and paste it into run directory.
4. **Check `01_input/01_project/00_setup/run-config.md`.**
      - operator `kyuhi`, 
      - machine `kyuhiPC`, 
      - plan `PRO`, 
      - permission mode `auto`, 
      - model `claude-opus-5-5`, 
      - effort `medium`
      - Run label: **change it for every run** (`kyuhi_single-agent_sdd_v006`, then `v006`,...).
      - Run ID: **keep empty it generates by itself**
      - Starting commit: **keep empty it generates by itself**
5. **Check the price row in `03_statistics/usage.md`.** It is pre-filled for Opus 5.5; change it only if the prices or the model changed.
6. **Create `.env`**: copy `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` to `.env` in the run folder and fill every value (database password, organizer login, NVD key). Never paste a secret into the chat.
7. **Commit the inputs**: `git add -A`, `git commit -m "initial commit"`. Check that `git status` does not list `.env` (it must be clean) before anything is pushed.
8. **Connect to the shared runs repository and push the initial setup** (so the start state is on record before the agent starts):
   ```bash
   git remote add origin https://github.com/SQA-interns/Structured_Input_Files.git
   git push -u origin kyuhi/single-agent/sdd/v006
   ```
   Use your own operator name in the branch. Every operator pushes to a branch of its own in this repository, never to `main`. Sign in to GitHub when asked. If `git remote add` says the remote already exists, check it with `git remote -v` and fix it with `git remote set-url origin https://github.com/SQA-interns/Structured_Input_Files.git`. Do not push before `.env` is confirmed absent from `git status`.
9. **Set the same permission mode** you set in `run-config.md`.
10. **Check the environment** (the same for all three operators): Docker Engine 29.8.1 and Compose 5.5.1, Node 24.13.0, Java 21, internet access for the scanners (NVD key in `.env`), no other heavy load on the machine during the run, one session only.

**If you are not kyuhi**, change only these lines in `01_input/01_project/00_setup/run-config.md` and nothing else (not the inputs, not the tools):

| Line | kyuhi | tanej | tjan |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operator | `kyuhi` | `tanej` | `tjan` |
| Machine | `kyuhiPC` | a label of your computer | a label of your computer |
| Plan | `PRO` | your plan | your plan |
| Run label | `kyuhi_single-agent_sdd_v006` | `tanej_single-agent_sdd_v006` | `tjan_single-agent_sdd_v006` |

## 2. Start the run
Open a **new agent session in the run folder** (only one session per run; do not open other sessions in this folder, the newest one is taken as the run's transcript) and send exactly:

```
Read AGENTS.md and start.
```

## 3. During the run
- Answer tooling and environment questions with the standard answers below, the same way in every run.
- The acceptance criteria, the end-to-end scenarios and the answers to the open questions are inputs, so the agent should not ask about business behaviour. If it does anyway, answer only: *"No further information is available. Choose the proposed default option and record it as a decision."*
- To **any other question not listed below**, give the same answer in every run: *"Choose the proposed default option and record it as a decision."* A frozen acceptance test that cannot pass (a defect in the test harness or in one assertion): approve the agent's proposed default fix (option 1). Do not add your own ideas or hints; different answers make the runs incomparable.
- The agent works until the **quality gate** is met (mutation score 90 %, line coverage 95 %, per component). Do not tell it to stop earlier or to go further.
- Type at least one line of each answer yourself; a pasted-only answer makes the agent ask you to confirm.
- Do not change the input files. Do not leave a question unanswered for more than an hour: the cache expires and the wait is excluded from the results, but the time is lost. If you must stop, tell the agent so it records the wait.

**Standard answers (conference registration project; decision numbers differ, recognise them by subject)**
| Phase | The agent asks about | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Host JDK, Node, npm or Docker differs from the pins by a patch version | No question: pre-approved (PA-05). Anything else (a different minor or major version): approve the installed version only if the agent says everything runs. |
| 0 | `vitest` or `jscpd` has Critical or High vulnerabilities | Move to the fixed versions the agent proposes (`jscpd` 5.4.0). `vitest` and `@vitest/coverage-v8` stay on 4.1.11: 5.x does not work with Stryker (see phase 6). No question if `tech-stack.md` already has them. |
| 0 | CVE-2025-7962 on `angus-activation`, CVE-2025-15104 on `hibernate-validator`, dev-only `npm audit` advisories | No question: pre-approved in `01_project/00_setup/pre-approved.md` (PA-01 to PA-03). If the agent asks anyway, answer: *use pre-approved.md*. |
| 6 | Semgrep "basic authentication" (High) on the organizer endpoint | No question: pre-approved (PA-04). If the agent asks anyway, answer: *use pre-approved.md*. |
| 6 | Stryker reports an implausibly low frontend score (about 25 %) or the agent says mutants are not activated | Approve `vitest` and `@vitest/coverage-v8` 4.1.x, the same version for both; `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` 10.0.0 does not work with Vitest 5. No question if `tech-stack.md` has 4.1.11. |

Anything the agent decides on its own (for example a scanner false positive rated Medium) needs no answer.

## 4. After the run
The measuring is automatic. `.claude/settings.json` in the run folder holds a status line script that keeps the harness's own usage numbers (`03_statistics/usage-snapshot.json`) and a hook that builds the report when the session ends (or about 8 seconds after the agent's last reply once the run has ended). Do not edit or delete `.claude/settings.json`. If Claude Code asks whether to trust the folder or its hooks, accept.
1. **Close the session** (`/exit`) once the agent has written the final statistics. Wait for the terminal to return: the hook then writes `03_statistics/results/` and `03_statistics/data/` and fills the empty cells of `usage.md` (cost, API time, wall time, plan limits) from the snapshot. `03_statistics/results/auto-report.log` shows what it did.
2. **Only if `results/run-report.html` is missing** (hook not run, session killed, folder not trusted): open a new session in the same folder and send exactly:

   ```
   Run node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics and report what it prints. Do not change anything else.

# Metrics

> Owner: Experiment lead · Read in: every phase and post-run · Agent: read-only

Experiment measurement only. Record observed values; never estimate. An unobservable value stays `null` with a `<field>Reason`.

Goal column: **↓** lower is better, **↑** higher is better, **=** should equal the stated value, **i** information for interpreting other numbers.

## Principles

- **Human waiting is not part of the result.** Agent time is wall time minus every wait for a human. A wait over one hour also lets the 1-hour prompt cache expire, and the call after it writes the whole context again; that rebuild is a cost of the wait, so `usage.costUsdExclWaits` removes it. Compare runs on agent time and `costUsdExclWaits`.
- **Record only what only you can see, and with the clock tool.** The agent records what happened (waits, loops, decisions, deviations, test and quality results). Timestamps come from `tools/stat.mjs`, never from memory or estimates. Everything that can be computed from the transcripts and git is computed after the run by `tools/build-report.mjs`, so the run spends no calls on it.
- **Make runs comparable.** Say what a number covers. Scope, level and tool of coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

## 1. Agent, during the run → `run-log.json`

Phase 0, first action: `node 03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs init`. It creates `run-log.json` from the template, a unique `runId`, the start time and commit, the transcript path and the environment. It prints what it wrote.

| Field | When | How | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId`, `model`, `effort`, `templateVersion`, `start`, `startCommit`, `transcript`, `environment` | phase 0 | written by `stat.mjs init` from `run-config.md`, git and the host | i |
| `phases[].start`, `phases[].end` | every phase boundary | `stat.mjs phase <n> start` and `stat.mjs phase <n> end`; a start also closes the previous phase, `phase 7 end` also sets `end` and `finalCommit` | ↓ agent time per phase |
| `humanInterventions[]` | every time the agent waits for the human or the human acts, including stops, restarts and installs | `stat.mjs wait start <cause> "<reason>" [decisionId]` when you ask or stop, `stat.mjs wait end` when work resumes. `cause`: `decision`, `environment`, `approval`, `session`, `other` | ↓ count and minutes; every minute here is excluded from agent time |
| `firstTestRun`, `finalTestRun` | first full run before fixes; last full run | edit the file: `passed`, `failed` and `byLevel` (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e` counts) | first: ↓ failed (defects the first run found); final: ↑ passed, `failed` = 0 |
| `acceptanceCriteria` | end of phase 3; changes in phase 4 | `total` criteria, `frozenTests`, `frozenTestChanges[]` as `{decisionId, reason}` | ↑ criteria covered by tests; ↓ frozen-test changes (each one needed a human) |
| `findings` | end of phase 6 | counts by severity, as found | ↓ |
| `openAtEnd` | end of phase 6 | Critical, High and Medium findings still open after triage | = 0 for Critical and High |
| `fixLoops[]` | each verify → fix → re-verify loop | `{loop, findings, category, needsHuman, change, start, end}`. `category`: `test-gap`, `security-config`, `dependency`, `defect`, `process`, `tooling`. `start` is the first fix action, `end` the clean re-check (UTC, `date -u +%FT%TZ`) | ↓ minutes per loop; a loop that repeats across runs belongs in the template |
| `decisions[]` | each decision record | `{id, type, phase, category, start, end}`; `type` `blocking` or `non-blocking`; `category`: `environment`, `dependency`, `security-finding`, `frozen-test`, `requirement`, `other`; `end` = when resolved | ↓ blocking; a category that repeats across runs can be answered in advance |

`commits[]` and `commitSummary` are not recorded by the agent: the post-run step reads them from `git log`.

## 2. Post-run session → `run-log.json`, `results/`, `data/`

Started after the run ends, in a new session whose only task is: "Run `node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics` and report what it prints. Do not change anything else." Before it, run `/cost` once in the finished session (the plan limits are then captured in the transcript). The script:

1. measures the run from the session transcript(s), the sub-agent transcripts next to them and `git log`, and stores `time`, `usage`, `environment`, `commits`, `commitSummary` in `run-log.json`;
2. copies the transcripts to `03_statistics/data/` (committed with the run, so the measuring can be repeated on any machine; the recorded path is used when it exists, the copy otherwise);

| Field | What it is | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| `time.agentMin` | sum over phases of wall time minus waits (recorded interventions and idle gaps above 10 minutes in the transcript) | ↓ |
| `time.humanWaitMin`, `time.waitsOver60Min`, `time.longWaits[]` | excluded waiting, and each wait over an hour with its cause | ↓; = 0 waits over an hour |
| `time.modelMin`, `time.toolMin` | transcript time spent generating and running tools | ↓; tool time shows what to automate or speed up |
| `time.unrecordedIdleMin` | idle time in the transcript that `humanInterventions` does not cover | = 0 (a recording gap) |
| `time.phaseChecks` | phase boundaries written by `stat.mjs` against typed ones, and implausible timestamps | all via `stat.mjs`, no issues |
| `time.byPhase[]` | wall, wait, agent, model and tool minutes per phase | ↓ in phases 0, 1, 2, 7 (overhead); phases 4 to 6 hold the real work |
| `usage.inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `thinkingTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `modelCalls` | sums over every model call, each call counted once, sub-agents included | ↓ |
| `usage.toolCalls` | total, errors, per tool name | ↓ calls and errors |
| `usage.costUsd` | tokens × the prices in `usage.md`, per model | ↓ |
| `usage.costUsdExclWaits` | `costUsd` minus the cache rebuilds that followed a wait over an hour | ↓ (the comparison figure) |
| `usage.cacheRebuilds[]` | each cache write above 150k tokens, the wait before it and its extra cost | = none caused by waits |
| `usage.subagents` | sub-agent calls, transcripts found, their cost (inside `costUsd`) | i; a call without a transcript is a measuring gap |
| `usage.panel`, `usage.check` | the harness's own totals (`cost-state`) and the difference to our calculation | difference within 1.5 % |
| `usage.byPhase[]` | calls, tokens, cost and average context per phase | ↓ in late phases, where context is largest |
| `usage.context` | peak and average context tokens per call, share of calls above 150k | ↓ (every call re-reads the whole context) |

| `environment` | operator, machine, plan, permission mode (from `run-config.md`), the host the run started on (account, CPU, memory, working directory; read by `stat.mjs init`), operating system and tool versions (at the start), harness version, entry point, models, effort and permission modes seen (from the transcripts), measuring host | i; needed to explain differences between runs |

Prices before the post-run session (one row per model id, shape as in the file). After it only `Approval prompts` is yours; the other cells are filled automatically when empty, and anything you wrote stays. A mismatch between the harness's total and our calculation is reported in the last row.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Every story has at least one AC in the given list | Pass: 8 stories, 35 criteria, none without a criterion; the count matches the traceability table and the stated total |

|---|---|---|

| G-2 | No maximum length is given for the text fields. | spec: field limits (SB-01, SR-03 body limit) |
| G-3 | "Valid email format" (BR-03) is not defined further. | spec: email rule |
| G-4 | The status code for the HTTPS-only refusal (AC-008-04) and for a storage failure (AC-005-03, "not 201") is not fixed. | spec: error model |
| G-5 | Rate-limit values and the request-size limit (SR-03) are not given. | spec: limits |
| G-6 | Whether emails are sent synchronously or after the response is not fixed; OQ-03 only fixes the order (after storage) and that failures keep the 201. | spec: notification flow |
| G-7 | The source of the organizer notification recipients, sender address and conference name is configuration (`environments.md`), but the email wording is not given. | spec: email content |

# Specification

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `project/02_design/*`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes

Contracts referenced below live in `docs/02_contracts/`. Versions are only in `tech-stack.md`.

## 1. System overview

Two components (`architecture.md`): **backend** (Spring Boot API, root package `si.konferenca.registration`) and **frontend** (React single page built with Vite, served by nginx). PostgreSQL stores registrations; a named volume holds the raw JSON copies; an SMTP server (Mailpit locally) receives the emails; Google reCAPTCHA v2 protects the registration (test mode locally and in tests).

```
browser ──/──► frontend (nginx: static files, /api proxy) ──/api──► backend ──► PostgreSQL
                                                                    ├──► JSON copy volume
                                                                    ├──► SMTP
                                                                    └──► reCAPTCHA siteverify (production)
```

The frontend calls only `/api/**` (AR-01). In production an external nginx terminates TLS, serves `/` from the frontend and forwards `/api` to the backend (`environments.md`).

## 2. Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03)

Declared style: **layered core with ports for side effects**. Packages under `si.konferenca.registration`:

| Package | Responsibility | May depend on (application packages) |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | registration types, option categories, conference catalog, submission, accepted registration, validation rules (pure Java, no Spring, no JPA) | none |
| `catalog` | loads and validates the conference configuration file at startup | `domain` |
| `service` | registration use case (validate, verify reCAPTCHA, store, write copy, notify); declares the ports `CaptchaVerifier`, `JsonCopyStore`, `RegistrationNotifier` | `domain`, `persistence` |
| `persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repository, mapping to `domain` | `domain` |
| `storage` | JSON copy files (implements `JsonCopyStore`) | `domain`, `service` |
| `mail` | participant and organizer emails (implements `RegistrationNotifier`) | `domain`, `service` |
| `captcha` | reCAPTCHA verification, test mode (implements `CaptchaVerifier`) | `domain`, `service` |
| `export` | Excel workbook of all registrations | `domain`, `persistence` |
| `security` | Spring Security, organizer Basic auth, HTTPS-only filter, rate limit and body-size filters, production start guard | `domain` |
| `web` | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, error mapping | `domain`, `catalog`, `service`, `export` |
| root | `RegistrationApplication` and `@ConfigurationProperties` (`RegistrationProperties`) | any |

ArchUnit rules (written in phase 5, checked in phase 6, DoD-04) check exactly this table:

1. `domain` depends on no other application package and on no `org.springframework..`, `jakarta.persistence..` class.
2. Each package depends only on the packages listed in its row (plus the root package for `RegistrationProperties`, JDK, and third-party libraries).
3. No package depends on `web` (except `web` itself).
4. `service` does not depend on `storage`, `mail` or `captcha` (ports invert the dependency).
5. No cycles between the packages above (slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..`, AR-03).

Justification: the use case must enforce the storage-before-response order (AR-05) and storage-before-email order (OQ-03) in one place (`service`); the side effects are behind ports so the order is testable and the adapters cannot call back into the web layer. Persistence is used directly by `service` because there is only one store and a port would add no checkable value.

## 3. Conference configuration (US-003, AR-04, BR-04, BR-05, OQ-01, OQ-02)

- One JSON file, schema `02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`, location from the setting `registration.conference-config` (env `REGISTRATION_CONFERENCE_CONFIG`; default `classpath:conference.json`, the shipped configuration, local and test only; the `prod` profile has no default).
- Contents: `options[]` (`id`, `name`, `category` ∈ `WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL`, `OTHER`, `active` default `true`, `availableTo` ⊆ {`EXTERNAL`, `STUDENT`} default both) and `consents[]` (`id`, `text`, `mandatory`).
- Loaded once at startup. The backend **refuses to start** (exception during context start, non-zero exit) when: the file is missing or not valid JSON; an option or consent id is duplicated, missing or does not match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`; a category or registration type is unknown; a name or consent text is missing or blank; `availableTo` is empty (AC-003-03).
- Changing the programme = editing this file and restarting; no code change and the participant fields are not configurable (BR-01, AC-003-02).
- Shipped configuration (`backend/src/main/resources/conference.json`): two workshops (one external-only), two events, two meals, one other activity, one inactive workshop, and the mandatory consent `privacy` with the OQ-02 wording.

## 4. REST API (contract `02_contracts/openapi.json`)

| Method and path | Access | Purpose | Responses |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/form-config` | public, rate limited | conference name, reCAPTCHA site key and test-mode flag, consents, **active** options with `id`, `name`, `category`, `availableTo` (AC-003-01, AC-003-02) | 200, 429 |
| `POST /api/registrations` | public, reCAPTCHA, rate limited, body ≤ 16 KiB | submit a registration | 201 `{id, registeredAt}`; 400 field errors; 413; 415; 429; 500 |
| `GET /api/organizer/registrations.xlsx` | organizer (HTTP Basic), HTTPS-only, rate limited | Excel export (US-008) | 200 workbook; 401; 403 (plain HTTP from non-localhost); 429 |

Health and readiness: `GET /actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` on the backend port, not routed by the proxies (NFR-04, ES-09). Nothing else of the actuator is exposed.

### 4.1 Registration request

JSON object with `type` (`EXTERNAL` | `STUDENT`), `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization` (external), `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId` (student), `optionIds` (array of strings, may be empty), `consents` (array of given consent ids), `recaptchaToken`. Unknown properties are rejected (400).

### 4.2 Validation (SB-01, BR-01..05, SR-01, SR-04; order of evaluation does not matter, all field errors are returned together)

| Field key | Rule | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | required, `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` | "Choose a registration type." |
| `firstName`, `lastName` | required after trimming; ≤ 100 characters | "This field is required." / "Use at most 100 characters." |
| `email` | required after trimming; ≤ 254 characters; matches `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` | "Enter a valid email address." |
| `organization` | EXTERNAL: required, ≤ 200; STUDENT: must be absent or empty | required / "This field does not apply to the registration type." |
| `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme` | STUDENT: required, ≤ 200; EXTERNAL: absent or empty | as above |
| `studentId` | STUDENT: required, ≤ 50; EXTERNAL: absent or empty | as above |
| `optionIds` | each id is a configured **active** option available to the type; no id twice; ≤ 100 entries | "Select only available options, each at most once." |
| `consents.<id>` | every mandatory consent id is in `consents`; unknown ids rejected under `consents` | "This consent is required." |
| `recaptchaToken` | present and accepted by the verifier | "Confirm that you are not a robot." |

Trimming: leading and trailing whitespace (`String.strip()`) is removed from every text field before validation and storage (BR-02, AC-001-03). Inner characters are kept as entered, including line breaks and markup (they are encoded on output, SR-05). Unicode is accepted (BR-03).

reCAPTCHA is verified only when the token is present; the result is added to the other field errors. Rejected submissions create no row, no copy and no email (AC-001-07, AC-002-06).

### 4.3 Error model (SB-07, ES-07)

Every error body is `{"message": "<user text>", "fieldErrors": {"<field key>": "<message>"}}` (`fieldErrors` empty when not a field problem). No stack traces, exception names, SQL or paths are returned.

| Situation | Status | Message |
|---|---|---|
| Field errors | 400 | "Please correct the marked fields." |
| Malformed JSON, unknown property, wrong type | 400 | "The request could not be read." |
| Body over 16 KiB | 413 | "The request is too large." |
| Content type not JSON | 415 | "The request could not be read." |
| Rate limit exceeded | 429 (+ `Retry-After`) | "Too many requests. Please try again later." |
| Organizer credentials missing or wrong | 401 (+ `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="organizer"`) | "Authentication required." |
| Organizer request over plain HTTP from a non-loopback client while HTTPS-only is on | 403 | "HTTPS is required." |
| Storage or copy failure, any unexpected error | 500 | "The registration could not be completed. Please try again later." |

## 5. Registration flow (BR-06, BR-07, AR-05, OQ-03, US-005..007)

1. Validate (4.2); verify reCAPTCHA; on any error answer 400.
2. In one database transaction: insert the registration, its options (id, name and category as configured at that moment) and consents (id, text, time given = registration time); flush; write the JSON copy `<id>.json` (write to a temporary file in the same directory, then atomic move). If writing the copy fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after the copy was written, the copy is deleted.
3. After the commit: send the participant confirmation, then one organizer notification per configured organizer address (attachment = the bytes of the stored copy). Each send failure is logged as `Email <kind> failed for registration <id>` with no personal data, and the registration stays accepted (OQ-03, AC-006-03).
4. Answer 201 with `{id, registeredAt}`.

`id` is a random UUID; `registeredAt` is UTC with millisecond precision. Several registrations with the same email are allowed (OQ-05).

## 6. Persistence (contract `02_contracts/database.sql`, AR-06, ES-08)

Flyway migration `V1__registration_schema.sql` is the contract file verbatim: tables `registration`, `registration_option`, `registration_consent`, text columns `varchar` (UTF-8 database), times `timestamptz`. `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`; schema changes only through new migrations. Data lives on the `pgdata` named volume (NFR-02). No automatic deletion (OQ-06); release notes tell the operator to delete rows and copies at the latest 12 months after the conference.

## 7. JSON copy (contract `02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json`)

UTF-8 file `<json-copy-dir>/<id>.json`, setting `registration.json-copy-dir` (env `REGISTRATION_JSON_COPY_DIR`, default `./data/json-copies`; containers `/data/json-copies` on the `jsoncopies` named volume). Contents: `id`, `type`, `registeredAt`, the type's own fields (trimmed), `options[]` (`id`, `name`, `category`), `consents[]` (`id`, `text`, `givenAt`). Non-ASCII characters are written as UTF-8, not escaped (NFR-01, AC-005-04). No internal fields (SR-07).

## 8. Emails (contract `02_contracts/emails.md`; SR-05, SR-07, US-006, US-007)

- Plain text (`text/plain; charset=UTF-8`) only; user input appears only in the body, never in a header. Subject lines contain only the configured conference name. The recipient header is built from the validated address alone (no display name). Markup is therefore literal text (AC-006-02).
- Participant confirmation: to the participant; names conference, participant and selected options.
- Organizer notification: one message per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated); body lists every submitted field, options and consents; attachment `registration-<id>.json` (`application/json`) equal to the stored copy (AC-007-02).
- Settings: `spring.mail.host`/`port` (env `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, defaults Mailpit `localhost:1025` for local/test only), `SMTP_USERNAME`/`SMTP_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_STARTTLS` (default off locally), sender `registration.mail.from` (default `registration@konferenca.si`), conference name `registration.conference-name`; connection and read timeouts 5 s.

## 9. reCAPTCHA (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05)

- Production path: `POST` form `secret`, `response`, `remoteip` to `registration.recaptcha.verify-url` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`); accepted only when the answer is HTTP 200 with `"success": true`. Timeouts or errors count as rejected.
- Test mode (`registration.recaptcha.test-mode`, env `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`, default **false**): no network call; exactly the token `test-mode-token` is accepted, every other token is rejected. The frontend shows a stand-in checkbox "I am not a robot (test mode)" instead of the Google widget and sends that token.
- Start guard (`prod` profile): the backend refuses to start when test mode is on, when `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` or `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` is empty, or when organizer HTTPS-only is off.
- Site key is delivered to the frontend through `GET /api/form-config` (AR-07); the secret key never leaves the backend.

## 10. Export (US-008, BR-08, SR-06, SR-07)

- `GET /api/organizer/registrations.xlsx`, HTTP Basic against `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` / `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (no defaults; the password is held only as a BCrypt hash after startup, SB-03). Stateless, no session, no CSRF token needed (no cookies).
- HTTPS-only filter runs before authentication: when `registration.organizer.https-only` (env `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY`, default **true**) is on and the request is not secure and the client address is not loopback, answer 403 and do not evaluate credentials (AC-008-04). The client address and scheme come from `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Forwarded-Proto` only when set by a trusted internal proxy (`server.forward-headers-strategy=native`, Tomcat's internal-proxy ranges).
- Workbook: one sheet "Registrations", header row then one row per registration ordered by registration time: Registration ID, Type, Registered at (UTC ISO-8601), First name, Last name, Email, Organization / institution, Study institution, Study programme, Student ID, Options (names joined by "; "), Consents (`<id> given <time>` joined by "; "). All cells are string cells (no formulas). `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`.

## 11. Security controls

| ID | Implementation |
|---|---|
| SB-01 | server-side validation 4.2 for every input, unknown JSON properties rejected, frontend checks only for usability |
| SB-02 | only the export is non-public; Spring Security requires role `ORGANIZER` on `/api/organizer/**`, everything else under `/api` explicitly permitted, all other paths denied except health |
| SB-03 | BCrypt hash of the organizer password created at startup; secrets only from env (ES-01, ES-02) |
| SB-04 | TLS at the external nginx in production; plain HTTP only on 127.0.0.1 locally; SR-06 filter |
| SB-05 | JPA parameter binding only; React escapes output; plain-text emails; string cells in Excel |
| SB-06, SR-03 | per-client fixed-window rate limits: form config 120/min, registrations 20/min, organizer export 10/min (also limits failed logins); configurable; body limit 16 KiB on `/api/**` (also `client_max_body_size 16k` in nginx) |
| SB-07, ES-07 | error model 4.3; logs carry registration ids only, never personal data or secrets; `server.error.include-*=never` |
| SB-08 | Dependency-Check and `npm audit` (phase 0 and phase 6) |
| SB-09 | Semgrep and gitleaks (phase 6) |
| SB-10 | API: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`; frontend nginx: CSP allowing self and Google reCAPTCHA hosts only, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy` |
| SB-11 | backend image runs as a non-root user; frontend nginx runs as user `nginx` on port 8080; PostgreSQL and Mailpit official images |
| SB-12, SB-13 | only the fields in `business-rules.md` are collected; purposes and retention as in `security-requirements.md` (OQ-06) |
| SB-14 | consent checkboxes are never preselected (UI contract); the backend requires each mandatory consent explicitly in `consents` and stores the time given |
| SR-01 | backend verification 9; frontend widget alone never accepted |
| SR-02 | test mode only by env, default off; `prod` start guard 9 |
| SR-04 | option ids checked against the active configured set and the registration type (4.2) |
| SR-05 | 8 |
| SR-06 | 10 |
| SR-07 | export and organizer email contain only the registration's fields, options, consents, id and time |
| SR-08 | frontend nginx sets `proxy_set_header Host` to the upstream name and overwrites `X-Forwarded-For` with `$remote_addr`; the production proxy setup in the release notes does the same |

CORS: no cross-origin access by default; `registration.cors.allowed-origins` (env `REGISTRATION_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`) may be set for local development only.

## 12. Frontend (contract `02_contracts/ui.md`; US-001, US-002, US-004, NFR-03)

- One page. On load it fetches `/api/form-config`. The participant chooses "External participant" or "Student"; the form then shows exactly that type's fields, the active options available to the type grouped into fieldsets Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities (empty groups hidden), the consent checkboxes (unchecked), the reCAPTCHA (Google widget with the configured site key, or the test-mode stand-in) and the button "Register".
- Before sending, the same rules as 4.2 for required fields, lengths and email format are checked in the browser; on any error the errors are shown next to the fields and no request is sent (AC-004-03).
- 201: the form is replaced by the confirmation (participant's name, selected option names) (AC-004-01).
- 400 with `fieldErrors`: each message next to its field, entered values kept, reCAPTCHA reset (AC-004-02).
- Any other status or a network failure: general message "The registration could not be completed. Please try again later." without technical details; values kept (AC-004-04).
- Built as static files; served by nginx, which proxies `/api/` to the backend (AR-01). No secret in the bundle (AR-07).

## 13. Configuration summary (ES-01; `environments.md`)

| Setting | Env variable | Default (where allowed) |
|---|---|---|
| Database URL, user | `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_USER` | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/registration`, `registration` (local/test; `prod` none) |
| Database password | `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | none |
| SMTP host, port, STARTTLS, user, password | `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_STARTTLS`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `localhost`, `1025`, `false` (local/test; `prod` host none) |
| Sender, conference name | `REGISTRATION_MAIL_FROM`, `REGISTRATION_CONFERENCE_NAME` | `registration@konferenca.si`, `Conference` |
| Organizer recipients | `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | none |
| Options source | `REGISTRATION_CONFERENCE_CONFIG` | `classpath:conference.json` (local/test; `prod` none) |
| JSON copy directory | `REGISTRATION_JSON_COPY_DIR` | `./data/json-copies` |
| reCAPTCHA test mode, keys, verify URL | `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`, `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | `false`, empty, empty, Google URL |
| Organizer login, HTTPS-only | `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | none, none, `true` |
| CORS origins | `REGISTRATION_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | empty |
| Rate limits, body limit | `REGISTRATION_RATE_LIMIT_*`, `REGISTRATION_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | 120 / 20 / 10 per minute, 16384 |

## 14. Deployment and local stack (NFR-02, NFR-04, ES-09, SB-11)

`02_output/docker-compose.yml`: `postgres` (volume `pgdata`, `pg_isready` health check), `mailpit` (SMTP 1025, UI/API 8025), `backend` (image from `backend/Dockerfile`: Maven build stage on the Temurin JDK image is not in the stack, so the jar is built with the wrapper on the host and copied into the `eclipse-temurin` JRE image; non-root; volume `jsoncopies`; health check on `/actuator/health/readiness`), `frontend` (multi-stage: `node` image builds, `nginx` image serves; health check on `/`). Every port is published on `127.0.0.1` only: frontend 8081, backend 8080, Mailpit 8025, PostgreSQL 5432. Secrets come from the repository-root `.env` through `env_file`. Local stack sets `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true` and `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false` (allowed on local plain HTTP only).

## 15. Quality requirements
