# Specification

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `project/02_design/*`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes

Contracts referenced below live in `docs/02_contracts/`. Versions are only in `tech-stack.md`.

## 1. System overview

Two components (`architecture.md`): **backend** (Spring Boot API, root package `si.konferenca.registration`) and **frontend** (React single page built with Vite, served by nginx). PostgreSQL stores registrations; a named volume holds the raw JSON copies; an SMTP server (Mailpit locally) receives the emails; Google reCAPTCHA v2 protects the registration (test mode locally and in tests).

```
browser ──/──► frontend (nginx: static files, /api proxy) ──/api──► backend ──► PostgreSQL
                                                                    ├──► JSON copy volume
                                                                    ├──► SMTP
                                                                    └──► reCAPTCHA siteverify (production)
```

The frontend calls only `/api/**` (AR-01). In production an external nginx terminates TLS, serves `/` from the frontend and forwards `/api` to the backend (`environments.md`).

## 2. Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03)

Declared style: **layered core with ports for side effects**. Packages under `si.konferenca.registration`:

| Package | Responsibility | May depend on (application packages) |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | registration types, option categories, conference catalog, submission, accepted registration, validation rules (pure Java, no Spring, no JPA) | none |
| `catalog` | loads and validates the conference configuration file at startup | `domain` |
| `service` | registration use case (validate, verify reCAPTCHA, store, write copy, notify); declares the ports `CaptchaVerifier`, `JsonCopyStore`, `RegistrationNotifier` | `domain`, `persistence` |
| `persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repository, mapping to `domain` | `domain` |
| `storage` | JSON copy files (implements `JsonCopyStore`) | `domain`, `service` |
| `mail` | participant and organizer emails (implements `RegistrationNotifier`) | `domain`, `service` |
| `captcha` | reCAPTCHA verification, test mode (implements `CaptchaVerifier`) | `domain`, `service` |
| `export` | Excel workbook of all registrations | `domain`, `persistence` |
| `security` | Spring Security, organizer Basic auth, HTTPS-only filter, rate limit and body-size filters, production start guard | `domain` |
| `web` | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, error mapping | `domain`, `catalog`, `service`, `export` |
| root | `RegistrationApplication` and `@ConfigurationProperties` (`RegistrationProperties`) | any |

ArchUnit rules (written in phase 5, checked in phase 6, DoD-04) check exactly this table:

1. `domain` depends on no other application package and on no `org.springframework..`, `jakarta.persistence..` class.
2. Each package depends only on the packages listed in its row (plus the root package for `RegistrationProperties`, JDK, and third-party libraries).
3. No package depends on `web` (except `web` itself).
4. `service` does not depend on `storage`, `mail` or `captcha` (ports invert the dependency).
5. No cycles between the packages above (slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..`, AR-03).

Justification: the use case must enforce the storage-before-response order (AR-05) and storage-before-email order (OQ-03) in one place (`service`); the side effects are behind ports so the order is testable and the adapters cannot call back into the web layer. Persistence is used directly by `service` because there is only one store and a port would add no checkable value.

## 3. Conference configuration (US-003, AR-04, BR-04, BR-05, OQ-01, OQ-02)

- One JSON file, schema `02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`, location from the setting `registration.conference-config` (env `REGISTRATION_CONFERENCE_CONFIG`; default `classpath:conference.json`, the shipped configuration, local and test only; the `prod` profile has no default).
- Contents: `options[]` (`id`, `name`, `category` ∈ `WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL`, `OTHER`, `active` default `true`, `availableTo` ⊆ {`EXTERNAL`, `STUDENT`} default both) and `consents[]` (`id`, `text`, `mandatory`).
- Loaded once at startup. The backend **refuses to start** (exception during context start, non-zero exit) when: the file is missing or not valid JSON; an option or consent id is duplicated, missing or does not match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`; a category or registration type is unknown; a name or consent text is missing or blank; `availableTo` is empty (AC-003-03).
- Changing the programme = editing this file and restarting; no code change and the participant fields are not configurable (BR-01, AC-003-02).
- Shipped configuration (`backend/src/main/resources/conference.json`): two workshops (one external-only), two events, two meals, one other activity, one inactive workshop, and the mandatory consent `privacy` with the OQ-02 wording.

## 4. REST API (contract `02_contracts/openapi.json`)

| Method and path | Access | Purpose | Responses |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/form-config` | public, rate limited | conference name, reCAPTCHA site key and test-mode flag, consents, **active** options with `id`, `name`, `category`, `availableTo` (AC-003-01, AC-003-02) | 200, 429 |
| `POST /api/registrations` | public, reCAPTCHA, rate limited, body ≤ 16 KiB | submit a registration | 201 `{id, registeredAt}`; 400 field errors; 413; 415; 429; 500 |
| `GET /api/organizer/registrations.xlsx` | organizer (HTTP Basic), HTTPS-only, rate limited | Excel export (US-008) | 200 workbook; 401; 403 (plain HTTP from non-localhost); 429 |

Health and readiness: `GET /actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` on the backend port, not routed by the proxies (NFR-04, ES-09). Nothing else of the actuator is exposed.

### 4.1 Registration request

JSON object with `type` (`EXTERNAL` | `STUDENT`), `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization` (external), `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId` (student), `optionIds` (array of strings, may be empty), `consents` (array of given consent ids), `recaptchaToken`. Unknown properties are rejected (400).

### 4.2 Validation (SB-01, BR-01..05, SR-01, SR-04; order of evaluation does not matter, all field errors are returned together)

| Field key | Rule | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | required, `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` | "Choose a registration type." |
| `firstName`, `lastName` | required after trimming; ≤ 100 characters | "This field is required." / "Use at most 100 characters." |
| `email` | required after trimming; ≤ 254 characters; matches `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` | "Enter a valid email address." |
| `organization` | EXTERNAL: required, ≤ 200; STUDENT: must be absent or empty | required / "This field does not apply to the registration type." |
| `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme` | STUDENT: required, ≤ 200; EXTERNAL: absent or empty | as above |
| `studentId` | STUDENT: required, ≤ 50; EXTERNAL: absent or empty | as above |
| `optionIds` | each id is a configured **active** option available to the type; no id twice; ≤ 100 entries | "Select only available options, each at most once." |
| `consents.<id>` | every mandatory consent id is in `consents`; unknown ids rejected under `consents` | "This consent is required." |
| `recaptchaToken` | present and accepted by the verifier | "Confirm that you are not a robot." |

Trimming: leading and trailing whitespace (`String.strip()`) is removed from every text field before validation and storage (BR-02, AC-001-03). Inner characters are kept as entered, including line breaks and markup (they are encoded on output, SR-05). Unicode is accepted (BR-03).

reCAPTCHA is verified only when the token is present; the result is added to the other field errors. Rejected submissions create no row, no copy and no email (AC-001-07, AC-002-06).

### 4.3 Error model (SB-07, ES-07)

Every error body is `{"message": "<user text>", "fieldErrors": {"<field key>": "<message>"}}` (`fieldErrors` empty when not a field problem). No stack traces, exception names, SQL or paths are returned.

| Situation | Status | Message |
|---|---|---|
| Field errors | 400 | "Please correct the marked fields." |
| Malformed JSON, unknown property, wrong type | 400 | "The request could not be read." |
| Body over 16 KiB | 413 | "The request is too large." |
| Content type not JSON | 415 | "The request could not be read." |
| Rate limit exceeded | 429 (+ `Retry-After`) | "Too many requests. Please try again later." |
| Organizer credentials missing or wrong | 401 (+ `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="organizer"`) | "Authentication required." |
| Organizer request over plain HTTP from a non-loopback client while HTTPS-only is on | 403 | "HTTPS is required." |
| Storage or copy failure, any unexpected error | 500 | "The registration could not be completed. Please try again later." |

## 5. Registration flow (BR-06, BR-07, AR-05, OQ-03, US-005..007)

1. Validate (4.2); verify reCAPTCHA; on any error answer 400.
2. In one database transaction: insert the registration, its options (id, name and category as configured at that moment) and consents (id, text, time given = registration time); flush; write the JSON copy `<id>.json` (write to a temporary file in the same directory, then atomic move). If writing the copy fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after the copy was written, the copy is deleted.
3. After the commit: send the participant confirmation, then one organizer notification per configured organizer address (attachment = the bytes of the stored copy). Each send failure is logged as `Email <kind> failed for registration <id>` with no personal data, and the registration stays accepted (OQ-03, AC-006-03).
4. Answer 201 with `{id, registeredAt}`.

`id` is a random UUID; `registeredAt` is UTC with millisecond precision. Several registrations with the same email are allowed (OQ-05).

## 6. Persistence (contract `02_contracts/database.sql`, AR-06, ES-08)

Flyway migration `V1__registration_schema.sql` is the contract file verbatim: tables `registration`, `registration_option`, `registration_consent`, text columns `varchar` (UTF-8 database), times `timestamptz`. `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`; schema changes only through new migrations. Data lives on the `pgdata` named volume (NFR-02). No automatic deletion (OQ-06); release notes tell the operator to delete rows and copies at the latest 12 months after the conference.

## 7. JSON copy (contract `02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json`)

UTF-8 file `<json-copy-dir>/<id>.json`, setting `registration.json-copy-dir` (env `REGISTRATION_JSON_COPY_DIR`, default `./data/json-copies`; containers `/data/json-copies` on the `jsoncopies` named volume). Contents: `id`, `type`, `registeredAt`, the type's own fields (trimmed), `options[]` (`id`, `name`, `category`), `consents[]` (`id`, `text`, `givenAt`). Non-ASCII characters are written as UTF-8, not escaped (NFR-01, AC-005-04). No internal fields (SR-07).

## 8. Emails (contract `02_contracts/emails.md`; SR-05, SR-07, US-006, US-007)

- Plain text (`text/plain; charset=UTF-8`) only; user input appears only in the body, never in a header. Subject lines contain only the configured conference name. The recipient header is built from the validated address alone (no display name). Markup is therefore literal text (AC-006-02).
- Participant confirmation: to the participant; names conference, participant and selected options.
- Organizer notification: one message per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated); body lists every submitted field, options and consents; attachment `registration-<id>.json` (`application/json`) equal to the stored copy (AC-007-02).
- Settings: `spring.mail.host`/`port` (env `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, defaults Mailpit `localhost:1025` for local/test only), `SMTP_USERNAME`/`SMTP_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_STARTTLS` (default off locally), sender `registration.mail.from` (default `registration@konferenca.si`), conference name `registration.conference-name`; connection and read timeouts 5 s.

## 9. reCAPTCHA (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05)

- Production path: `POST` form `secret`, `response`, `remoteip` to `registration.recaptcha.verify-url` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`); accepted only when the answer is HTTP 200 with `"success": true`. Timeouts or errors count as rejected.
- Test mode (`registration.recaptcha.test-mode`, env `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`, default **false**): no network call; exactly the token `test-mode-token` is accepted, every other token is rejected. The frontend shows a stand-in checkbox "I am not a robot (test mode)" instead of the Google widget and sends that token.
- Start guard (`prod` profile): the backend refuses to start when test mode is on, when `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` or `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` is empty, or when organizer HTTPS-only is off.
- Site key is delivered to the frontend through `GET /api/form-config` (AR-07); the secret key never leaves the backend.

## 10. Export (US-008, BR-08, SR-06, SR-07)

- `GET /api/organizer/registrations.xlsx`, HTTP Basic against `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` / `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (no defaults; the password is held only as a BCrypt hash after startup, SB-03). Stateless, no session, no CSRF token needed (no cookies).
- HTTPS-only filter runs before authentication: when `registration.organizer.https-only` (env `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY`, default **true**) is on and the request is not secure and the client address is not loopback, answer 403 and do not evaluate credentials (AC-008-04). The client address and scheme come from `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Forwarded-Proto` only when set by a trusted internal proxy (`server.forward-headers-strategy=native`, Tomcat's internal-proxy ranges).
- Workbook: one sheet "Registrations", header row then one row per registration ordered by registration time: Registration ID, Type, Registered at (UTC ISO-8601), First name, Last name, Email, Organization / institution, Study institution, Study programme, Student ID, Options (names joined by "; "), Consents (`<id> given <time>` joined by "; "). All cells are string cells (no formulas). `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`.

## 11. Security controls

| ID | Implementation |
|---|---|
| SB-01 | server-side validation 4.2 for every input, unknown JSON properties rejected, frontend checks only for usability |
| SB-02 | only the export is non-public; Spring Security requires role `ORGANIZER` on `/api/organizer/**`, everything else under `/api` explicitly permitted, all other paths denied except health |
| SB-03 | BCrypt hash of the organizer password created at startup; secrets only from env (ES-01, ES-02) |
| SB-04 | TLS at the external nginx in production; plain HTTP only on 127.0.0.1 locally; SR-06 filter |
| SB-05 | JPA parameter binding only; React escapes output; plain-text emails; string cells in Excel |
| SB-06, SR-03 | per-client fixed-window rate limits: form config 120/min, registrations 20/min, organizer export 10/min (also limits failed logins); configurable; body limit 16 KiB on `/api/**` (also `client_max_body_size 16k` in nginx) |
| SB-07, ES-07 | error model 4.3; logs carry registration ids only, never personal data or secrets; `server.error.include-*=never` |
| SB-08 | Dependency-Check and `npm audit` (phase 0 and phase 6) |
| SB-09 | Semgrep and gitleaks (phase 6) |
| SB-10 | API: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`; frontend nginx: CSP allowing self and Google reCAPTCHA hosts only, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy` |
| SB-11 | backend image runs as a non-root user; frontend nginx runs as user `nginx` on port 8080; PostgreSQL and Mailpit official images |
| SB-12, SB-13 | only the fields in `business-rules.md` are collected; purposes and retention as in `security-requirements.md` (OQ-06) |
| SB-14 | consent checkboxes are never preselected (UI contract); the backend requires each mandatory consent explicitly in `consents` and stores the time given |
| SR-01 | backend verification 9; frontend widget alone never accepted |
| SR-02 | test mode only by env, default off; `prod` start guard 9 |
| SR-04 | option ids checked against the active configured set and the registration type (4.2) |
| SR-05 | 8 |
| SR-06 | 10 |
| SR-07 | export and organizer email contain only the registration's fields, options, consents, id and time |
| SR-08 | frontend nginx sets `proxy_set_header Host` to the upstream name and overwrites `X-Forwarded-For` with `$remote_addr`; the production proxy setup in the release notes does the same |

CORS: no cross-origin access by default; `registration.cors.allowed-origins` (env `REGISTRATION_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`) may be set for local development only.

## 12. Frontend (contract `02_contracts/ui.md`; US-001, US-002, US-004, NFR-03)

- One page. On load it fetches `/api/form-config`. The participant chooses "External participant" or "Student"; the form then shows exactly that type's fields, the active options available to the type grouped into fieldsets Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities (empty groups hidden), the consent checkboxes (unchecked), the reCAPTCHA (Google widget with the configured site key, or the test-mode stand-in) and the button "Register".
- Before sending, the same rules as 4.2 for required fields, lengths and email format are checked in the browser; on any error the errors are shown next to the fields and no request is sent (AC-004-03).
- 201: the form is replaced by the confirmation (participant's name, selected option names) (AC-004-01).
- 400 with `fieldErrors`: each message next to its field, entered values kept, reCAPTCHA reset (AC-004-02).
- Any other status or a network failure: general message "The registration could not be completed. Please try again later." without technical details; values kept (AC-004-04).
- Built as static files; served by nginx, which proxies `/api/` to the backend (AR-01). No secret in the bundle (AR-07).

## 13. Configuration summary (ES-01; `environments.md`)

| Setting | Env variable | Default (where allowed) |
|---|---|---|
| Database URL, user | `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_USER` | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/registration`, `registration` (local/test; `prod` none) |
| Database password | `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | none |
| SMTP host, port, STARTTLS, user, password | `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_STARTTLS`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `localhost`, `1025`, `false` (local/test; `prod` host none) |
| Sender, conference name | `REGISTRATION_MAIL_FROM`, `REGISTRATION_CONFERENCE_NAME` | `registration@konferenca.si`, `Conference` |
| Organizer recipients | `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | none |
| Options source | `REGISTRATION_CONFERENCE_CONFIG` | `classpath:conference.json` (local/test; `prod` none) |
| JSON copy directory | `REGISTRATION_JSON_COPY_DIR` | `./data/json-copies` |
| reCAPTCHA test mode, keys, verify URL | `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`, `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | `false`, empty, empty, Google URL |
| Organizer login, HTTPS-only | `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | none, none, `true` |
| CORS origins | `REGISTRATION_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | empty |
| Rate limits, body limit | `REGISTRATION_RATE_LIMIT_*`, `REGISTRATION_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | 120 / 20 / 10 per minute, 16384 |

`02_output/docker-compose.yml`: `postgres` (volume `pgdata`, `pg_isready` health check), `mailpit` (SMTP 1025, UI/API 8025), `backend` (image from `backend/Dockerfile`: Maven build stage on the Temurin JDK image is not in the stack, so the jar is built with the wrapper on the host and copied into the `eclipse-temurin` JRE image; non-root; volume `jsoncopies`; health check on `/actuator/health/readiness`), `frontend` (multi-stage: `node` image builds, `nginx` image serves; health check on `/`). ## 3. Conference configuration (US-003, AR-04, BR-04, BR-05, OQ-01, OQ-02)

- One JSON file, schema `02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`, location from the setting `registration.conference-config` (env `REGISTRATION_CONFERENCE_CONFIG`; default `classpath:conference.json`, the shipped configuration, local and test only; the `prod` profile has no default).
- Contents: `options[]` (`id`, `name`, `category` ∈ `WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL`, `OTHER`, `active` default `true`, `availableTo` ⊆ {`EXTERNAL`, `STUDENT`} default both) and `consents[]` (`id`, `text`, `mandatory`).
- Loaded once at startup. The backend **refuses to start** (exception during context start, non-zero exit) when: the file is missing or not valid JSON; an option or consent id is duplicated, missing or does not match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`; a category or registration type is unknown; a name or consent text is missing or blank; `availableTo` is empty (AC-003-03).
- Changing the programme = editing this file and restarting; no code change and the participant fields are not configurable (BR-01, AC-003-02).
- Shipped configuration (`backend/src/main/resources/conference.json`): two workshops (one external-only), two events, two meals, one other activity, one inactive workshop, and the mandatory consent `privacy` with the OQ-02 wording.

## 4. REST API (contract `02_contracts/openapi.json`)

| Method and path | Access | Purpose | Responses |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/form-config` | public, rate limited | conference name, reCAPTCHA site key and test-mode flag, consents, **active** options with `id`, `name`, `category`, `availableTo` (AC-003-01, AC-003-02) | 200, 429 |
| `POST /api/registrations` | public, reCAPTCHA, rate limited, body ≤ 16 KiB | submit a registration | 201 `{id, registeredAt}`; 400 field errors; 413; 415; 429; 500 |
| `GET /api/organizer/registrations.xlsx` | organizer (HTTP Basic), HTTPS-only, rate limited | Excel export (US-008) | 200 workbook; 401; 403 (plain HTTP from non-localhost); 429 |

Health and readiness: `GET /actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` on the backend port, not routed by the proxies (NFR-04, ES-09). Nothing else of the actuator is exposed.

### 4.1 Registration request

JSON object with `type` (`EXTERNAL` | `STUDENT`), `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization` (external), `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId` (student), `optionIds` (array of strings, may be empty), `consents` (array of given consent ids), `recaptchaToken`. Unknown properties are rejected (400).

### 4.2 Validation (SB-01, BR-01..05, SR-01, SR-04; order of evaluation does not matter, all field errors are returned together)

| Field key | Rule | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | required, `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` | "Choose a registration type." |
| `firstName`, `lastName` | required after trimming; ≤ 100 characters | "This field is required." / "Use at most 100 characters." |
| `email` | required after trimming; ≤ 254 characters; matches `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` | "Enter a valid email address." |
| `organization` | EXTERNAL: required, ≤ 200; STUDENT: must be absent or empty | required / "This field does not apply to the registration type." |
| `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme` | STUDENT: required, ≤ 200; EXTERNAL: absent or empty | as above |
| `studentId` | STUDENT: required, ≤ 50; EXTERNAL: absent or empty | as above |
| `optionIds` | each id is a configured **active** option available to the type; no id twice; ≤ 100 entries | "Select only available options, each at most once." |
| `consents.<id>` | every mandatory consent id is in `consents`; unknown ids rejected under `consents` | "This consent is required." |
| `recaptchaToken` | present and accepted by the verifier | "Confirm that you are not a robot." |

Trimming: leading and trailing whitespace (`String.strip()`) is removed from every text field before validation and storage (BR-02, AC-001-03). Inner characters are kept as entered, including line breaks and markup (they are encoded on output, SR-05). Unicode is accepted (BR-03).

reCAPTCHA is verified only when the token is present; the result is added to the other field errors. Rejected submissions create no row, no copy and no email (AC-001-07, AC-002-06).

### 4.3 Error model (SB-07, ES-07)

Every error body is `{"message": "<user text>", "fieldErrors": {"<field key>": "<message>"}}` (`fieldErrors` empty when not a field problem). No stack traces, exception names, SQL or paths are returned.

| Situation | Status | Message |
|---|---|---|
| Field errors | 400 | "Please correct the marked fields." |
| Malformed JSON, unknown property, wrong type | 400 | "The request could not be read." |
| Body over 16 KiB | 413 | "The request is too large." |
| Content type not JSON | 415 | "The request could not be read." |
| Rate limit exceeded | 429 (+ `Retry-After`) | "Too many requests. Please try again later." |
| Organizer credentials missing or wrong | 401 (+ `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="organizer"`) | "Authentication required." |
| Organizer request over plain HTTP from a non-loopback client while HTTPS-only is on | 403 | "HTTPS is required." |
| Storage or copy failure, any unexpected error | 500 | "The registration could not be completed. Please try again later." |

## 5. Registration flow (BR-06, BR-07, AR-05, OQ-03, US-005..007)

1. Validate (4.2); verify reCAPTCHA; on any error answer 400.
2. In one database transaction: insert the registration, its options (id, name and category as configured at that moment) and consents (id, text, time given = registration time); flush; write the JSON copy `<id>.json` (write to a temporary file in the same directory, then atomic move). If writing the copy fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after the copy was written, the copy is deleted.
3. After the commit: send the participant confirmation, then one organizer notification per configured organizer address (attachment = the bytes of the stored copy). Each send failure is logged as `Email <kind> failed for registration <id>` with no personal data, and the registration stays accepted (OQ-03, AC-006-03).
4. Answer 201 with `{id, registeredAt}`.

`id` is a random UUID; `registeredAt` is UTC with millisecond precision. Several registrations with the same email are allowed (OQ-05).

## 6. Persistence (contract `02_contracts/database.sql`, AR-06, ES-08)

Flyway migration `V1__registration_schema.sql` is the contract file verbatim: tables `registration`, `registration_option`, `registration_consent`, text columns `varchar` (UTF-8 database), times `timestamptz`. `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`; schema changes only through new migrations. Data lives on the `pgdata` named volume (NFR-02). No automatic deletion (OQ-06); release notes tell the operator to delete rows and copies at the latest 12 months after the conference.

## 7. JSON copy (contract `02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json`)

UTF-8 file `<json-copy-dir>/<id>.json`, setting `registration.json-copy-dir` (env `REGISTRATION_JSON_COPY_DIR`, default `./data/json-copies`; containers `/data/json-copies` on the `jsoncopies` named volume). Contents: `id`, `type`, `registeredAt`, the type's own fields (trimmed), `options[]` (`id`, `name`, `category`), `consents[]` (`id`, `text`, `givenAt`). Non-ASCII characters are written as UTF-8, not escaped (NFR-01, AC-005-04). No internal fields (SR-07).

## 8. Emails (contract `02_contracts/emails.md`; SR-05, SR-07, US-006, US-007)

- Plain text (`text/plain; charset=UTF-8`) only; user input appears only in the body, never in a header. Subject lines contain only the configured conference name. The recipient header is built from the validated address alone (no display name). Markup is therefore literal text (AC-006-02).
- Participant confirmation: to the participant; names conference, participant and selected options.
- Organizer notification: one message per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated); body lists every submitted field, options and consents; attachment `registration-<id>.json` (`application/json`) equal to the stored copy (AC-007-02).
- Settings: `spring.mail.host`/`port` (env `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, defaults Mailpit `localhost:1025` for local/test only), `SMTP_USERNAME`/`SMTP_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_STARTTLS` (default off locally), sender `registration.mail.from` (default `registration@konferenca.si`), conference name `registration.conference-name`; connection and read timeouts 5 s.

## 9. reCAPTCHA (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05)

- Production path: `POST` form `secret`, `response`, `remoteip` to `registration.recaptcha.verify-url` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`); accepted only when the answer is HTTP 200 with `"success": true`. Timeouts or errors count as rejected.
- Test mode (`registration.recaptcha.test-mode`, env `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`, default **false**): no network call; exactly the token `test-mode-token` is accepted, every other token is rejected. The frontend shows a stand-in checkbox "I am not a robot (test mode)" instead of the Google widget and sends that token.
- Start guard (`prod` profile): the backend refuses to start when test mode is on, when `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` or `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` is empty, or when organizer HTTPS-only is off.
- Site key is delivered to the frontend through `GET /api/form-config` (AR-07); the secret key never leaves the backend.

## 10. Export (US-008, BR-08, SR-06, SR-07)

- `GET /api/organizer/registrations.xlsx`, HTTP Basic against `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` / `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (no defaults; the password is held only as a BCrypt hash after startup, SB-03). Stateless, no session, no CSRF token needed (no cookies).
- HTTPS-only filter runs before authentication: when `registration.organizer.https-only` (env `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY`, default **true**) is on and the request is not secure and the client address is not loopback, answer 403 and do not evaluate credentials (AC-008-04). The client address and scheme come from `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Forwarded-Proto` only when set by a trusted internal proxy (`server.forward-headers-strategy=native`, Tomcat's internal-proxy ranges).
- Workbook: one sheet "Registrations", header row then one row per registration ordered by registration time: Registration ID, Type, Registered at (UTC ISO-8601), First name, Last name, Email, Organization / institution, Study institution, Study programme, Student ID, Options (names joined by "; "), Consents (`<id> given <time>` joined by "; "). All cells are string cells (no formulas). `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`.

## 12. Frontend (contract `02_contracts/ui.md`; US-001, US-002, US-004, NFR-03)

- One page. On load it fetches `/api/form-config`. The participant chooses "External participant" or "Student"; the form then shows exactly that type's fields, the active options available to the type grouped into fieldsets Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities (empty groups hidden), the consent checkboxes (unchecked), the reCAPTCHA (Google widget with the configured site key, or the test-mode stand-in) and the button "Register".
- Before sending, the same rules as 4.2 for required fields, lengths and email format are checked in the browser; on any error the errors are shown next to the fields and no request is sent (AC-004-03).
- 201: the form is replaced by the confirmation (participant's name, selected option names) (AC-004-01).
- 400 with `fieldErrors`: each message next to its field, entered values kept, reCAPTCHA reset (AC-004-02).
- Any other status or a network failure: general message "The registration could not be completed. Please try again later." without technical details; values kept (AC-004-04).
- Built as static files; served by nginx, which proxies `/api/` to the backend (AR-01). No secret in the bundle (AR-07).

+Trimming: leading and trailing whitespace (`String.strip()`) is removed from every text field before validation and storage (BR-02, AC-001-03). Inner characters are kept as entered, including line breaks and markup (they are encoded on output, SR-05). Unicode is accepted (BR-03).
+reCAPTCHA is verified only when the token is present; the result is added to the other field errors. Rejected submissions create no row, no copy and no email (AC-001-07, AC-002-06).

+Every error body is `{"message": "<user text>", "fieldErrors": {"<field key>": "<message>"}}` (`fieldErrors` empty when not a field problem). No stack traces, exception names, SQL or paths are returned.
+| Field errors | 400 | "Please correct the marked fields." |
+| Malformed JSON, unknown property, wrong type | 400 | "The request could not be read." |
+| Body over 16 KiB | 413 | "The request is too large." |
+| Content type not JSON | 415 | "The request could not be read." |
+| Rate limit exceeded | 429 (+ `Retry-After`) | "Too many requests. Please try again later." |
+| Organizer credentials missing or wrong | 401 (+ `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="organizer"`) | "Authentication required." |
+| Organizer request over plain HTTP from a non-loopback client while HTTPS-only is on | 403 | "HTTPS is required." |
+| Storage or copy failure, any unexpected error | 500 | "The registration could not be completed. Please try again later." |
+## 5. Registration flow (BR-06, BR-07, AR-05, OQ-03, US-005..007)
+1. Validate (4.2); verify reCAPTCHA; on any error answer 400.

+2. In one database transaction: insert the registration, its options (id, name and category as configured at that moment) and consents (id, text, time given = registration time); flush; write the JSON copy `<id>.json` (write to a temporary file in the same directory, then atomic move). If writing the copy fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after the copy was written, the copy is deleted.

+3. After the commit: send the participant confirmation, then one organizer notification per configured organizer address (attachment = the bytes of the stored copy). Each send failure is logged as `Email <kind> failed for registration <id>` with no personal data, and the registration stays accepted (OQ-03, AC-006-03).
+`id` is a random UUID; `registeredAt` is UTC with millisecond precision. Several registrations with the same email are allowed (OQ-05).

+Flyway migration `V1__registration_schema.sql` is the contract file verbatim: tables `registration`, `registration_option`, `registration_consent`, text columns `varchar` (UTF-8 database), times `timestamptz`. `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`; schema changes only through new migrations. Data lives on the `pgdata` named volume (NFR-02). No automatic deletion (OQ-06); release notes tell the operator to delete rows and copies at the latest 12 months after the conference.

+UTF-8 file `<json-copy-dir>/<id>.json`, setting `registration.json-copy-dir` (env `REGISTRATION_JSON_COPY_DIR`, default `./data/json-copies`; containers `/data/json-copies` on the `jsoncopies` named volume). Contents: `id`, `type`, `registeredAt`, the type's own fields (trimmed), `options[]` (`id`, `name`, `category`), `consents[]` (`id`, `text`, `givenAt`). Non-ASCII characters are written as UTF-8, not escaped (NFR-01, AC-005-04). No internal fields (SR-07).

+- Plain text (`text/plain; charset=UTF-8`) only; user input appears only in the body, never in a header. Subject lines contain only the configured conference name. The recipient header is built from the validated address alone (no display name). Markup is therefore literal text (AC-006-02).
+- Participant confirmation: to the participant; names conference, participant and selected options.

+- Organizer notification: one message per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated); body lists every submitted field, options and consents; attachment `registration-<id>.json` (`application/json`) equal to the stored copy (AC-007-02).

+- Settings: `spring.mail.host`/`port` (env `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, defaults Mailpit `localhost:1025` for local/test only), `SMTP_USERNAME`/`SMTP_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_STARTTLS` (default off locally), sender `registration.mail.from` (default `registration@konferenca.si`), conference name `registration.conference-name`; connection and read timeouts 5 s.

+- Production path: `POST` form `secret`, `response`, `remoteip` to `registration.recaptcha.verify-url` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`); accepted only when the answer is HTTP 200 with `"success": true`. Timeouts or errors count as rejected.

+- Test mode (`registration.recaptcha.test-mode`, env `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`, default **false**): no network call; exactly the token `test-mode-token` is accepted, every other token is rejected. The frontend shows a stand-in checkbox "I am not a robot (test mode)" instead of the Google widget and sends that token.
+- Start guard (`prod` profile): the backend refuses to start when test mode is on, when `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` or `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` is empty, or when organizer HTTPS-only is off.
+- Site key is delivered to the frontend through `GET /api/form-config` (AR-07); the secret key never leaves the backend.

+- `GET /api/organizer/registrations.xlsx`, HTTP Basic against `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` / `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (no defaults; the password is held only as a BCrypt hash after startup, SB-03). Stateless, no session, no CSRF token needed (no cookies).

+- HTTPS-only filter runs before authentication: when `registration.organizer.https-only` (env `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY`, default **true**) is on and the request is not secure and the client address is not loopback, answer 403 and do not evaluate credentials (AC-008-04). The client address and scheme come from `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Forwarded-Proto` only when set by a trusted internal proxy (`server.forward-headers-strategy=native`, Tomcat's internal-proxy ranges).

+- Workbook: one sheet "Registrations", header row then one row per registration ordered by registration time: Registration ID, Type, Registered at (UTC ISO-8601), First name, Last name, Email, Organization / institution, Study institution, Study programme, Student ID, Options (names joined by "; "), Consents (`<id> given <time>` joined by "; "). All cells are string cells (no formulas). `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`.
+| SB-01 | server-side validation 4.2 for every input, unknown JSON properties rejected, frontend checks only for usability |
+| SB-02 | only the export is non-public; Spring Security requires role `ORGANIZER` on `/api/organizer/**`, everything else under `/api` explicitly permitted, all other paths denied except health |
+| SB-03 | BCrypt hash of the organizer password created at startup; secrets only from env (ES-01, ES-02) |
+| SB-04 | TLS at the external nginx in production; plain HTTP only on 127.0.0.1 locally; SR-06 filter |
+| SB-05 | JPA parameter binding only; React escapes output; plain-text emails; string cells in Excel |

+| SB-06, SR-03 | per-client fixed-window rate limits: form config 120/min, registrations 20/min, organizer export 10/min (also limits failed logins); configurable; body limit 16 KiB on `/api/**` (also `client_max_body_size 16k` in nginx) |
+| SB-07, ES-07 | error model 4.3; logs carry registration ids only, never personal data or secrets; `server.error.include-*=never` |
+| SB-08 | Dependency-Check and `npm audit` (phase 0 and phase 6) |

+| SB-10 | API: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`; frontend nginx: CSP allowing self and Google reCAPTCHA hosts only, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy` |

+| SR-02 | test mode only by env, default off; `prod` start guard 9 |
+| SR-04 | option ids checked against the active configured set and the registration type (4.2) |
+| SR-07 | export and organizer email contain only the registration's fields, options, consents, id and time |

+CORS: no cross-origin access by default; `registration.cors.allowed-origins` (env `REGISTRATION_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`) may be set for local development only.

+- One page. On load it fetches `/api/form-config`. The participant chooses "External participant" or "Student"; the form then shows exactly that type's fields, the active options available to the type grouped into fieldsets Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities (empty groups hidden), the consent checkboxes (unchecked), the reCAPTCHA (Google widget with the configured site key, or the test-mode stand-in) and the button "Register".

+- Before sending, the same rules as 4.2 for required fields, lengths and email format are checked in the browser; on any error the errors are shown next to the fields and no request is sent (AC-004-03).
+- 201: the form is replaced by the confirmation (participant's name, selected option names) (AC-004-01).
+- 400 with `fieldErrors`: each message next to its field, entered values kept, reCAPTCHA reset (AC-004-02).
+- Any other status or a network failure: general message "The registration could not be completed. Please try again later." without technical details; values kept (AC-004-04).
+- Built as static files; served by nginx, which proxies `/api/` to the backend (AR-01). No secret in the bundle (AR-07).

# Email contract (backend → SMTP)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: spec section 8, US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07 · Agent: writes

Both messages are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist (spec section 5). A send failure is logged with the registration id only and does not change the API answer (OQ-03).

## Common rules

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| From | `registration.mail.from` (default `registration@konferenca.si`) |
| Recipients | exactly one `To` address per message, built from the address alone (no display name); no `Cc`, no `Bcc` |
| Subject | fixed text plus the configured conference name; never contains user input |
| Body | `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`; no HTML part; user input appears only here, as literal text |
| Headers | no header contains user input (SR-05) |

## Participant confirmation (US-006)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| To | the participant's email (trimmed, validated) |
| Subject | `Registration confirmed: <conference name>` |
| Body | see template |

```
Dear <firstName> <lastName>,

thank you for registering for <conference name>. Your registration has been received.

Registration type: <External participant | Student>
Selected options:
- <option name> (<Workshop | Event | Meal | Other activity>)
...                       (or the single line "- none")

Registration ID: <id>
```

## Organizer notification (US-007)

One message per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated, blanks ignored).

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| To | one organizer address |
| Subject | `New registration: <conference name>` |
| Structure | `multipart/mixed`: the text body, then one attachment |
| Attachment | file name `registration-<id>.json`, content type `application/json`, content byte-for-byte equal to the stored JSON copy `<id>.json` (AC-007-02) |
| Body | see template; only registration data (SR-07) |

```
A new registration was received for <conference name>.

Registration ID: <id>
Registered at: <registeredAt, ISO-8601 UTC>
Type: <EXTERNAL | STUDENT>
First name: <firstName>
Last name: <lastName>
Email: <email>
Organization / institution: <organization>      (EXTERNAL)
Study institution: <studyInstitution>           (STUDENT)
Study programme: <studyProgramme>               (STUDENT)
Student ID: <studentId>                         (STUDENT)
Options:
- <option name> (<category label>)              (or "- none")
Consents:
- <consent id>: given <givenAt>

The raw registration is attached as JSON.
```

# UI contract (participant ↔ frontend)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: spec section 12, US-001, US-002, US-004, NFR-03, BR-05 · Agent: writes

The accessible names below are the public interface the component and end-to-end tests use. Text is English.

## Page states

| State | What is shown |
|---|---|
| Loading | text "Loading…" until `GET /api/form-config` answers |
| Config failed | `role="alert"`: "The registration form is currently unavailable. Please try again later." |
| Form | heading (level 1) = conference name; a `form` with accessible name "Registration form" |
| Confirmation | after 201 only (BR-06): the form is removed; a region `role="status"` with heading "Registration received", the text "Thank you, <first name> <last name>.", and a list with accessible name "Selected options" holding one item per selected option name (or the text "No options selected.") |

## Form

| Element | Accessible name | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Registration type | radio group "Registration type" with radios "External participant" (value `EXTERNAL`) and "Student" (value `STUDENT`) | none preselected; fields and options appear only after a choice |
| Common fields | text inputs "First name", "Last name", "Email" (type `email` is not used, so the browser does not pre-empt the app's validation) | |
| External fields | "Organization / institution" | shown only for External participant |
| Student fields | "Study institution", "Study programme", "Student ID" | shown only for Student |
| Options | one `fieldset` per non-empty category, legends "Workshops", "Events", "Meals", "Other activities", in that order; one checkbox per active option available to the chosen type, labelled with the option name | all unchecked initially; options of other types are not rendered |
| Consents | one checkbox per configured consent, labelled with the consent text | never preselected (BR-05, SB-14) |
| reCAPTCHA | test mode (`recaptchaTestMode: true`): checkbox "I am not a robot (test mode)"; checked → token `test-mode-token`. Otherwise the Google v2 widget rendered with `recaptchaSiteKey` | reset after every failed submission |
| Submit | button "Register" | disabled while the request is in flight |

## Field errors (NFR-03, AC-004-02, AC-004-03)

- Field keys are those of the API (`firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization`, `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`, `optionIds`, `consents.<id>`, `recaptchaToken`, `type`).
- An error for a field is shown in an element with id `<key>-error` placed directly after the field (after the options fieldsets for `optionIds`; after the consent checkbox for `consents.<id>`; after the reCAPTCHA for `recaptchaToken`). The field has `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby="<key>-error"`, so its accessible description is the message. For `optionIds` the description is set on every option checkbox.
- Client-side checks before sending (same rules as the API, spec 4.2): type chosen; required fields not blank after trimming; length limits; email pattern `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$`; every mandatory consent checked; reCAPTCHA completed. Messages: "This field is required.", "Enter a valid email address.", "Use at most <n> characters.", "This consent is required.", "Confirm that you are not a robot.", "Choose a registration type.". When any check fails, no request is sent.
- Backend field errors (400) are shown with the backend's message text, next to their fields; all entered values stay.

## General errors (AC-004-04)

Any answer other than 201 or 400-with-field-errors, or a network failure: `role="alert"` with exactly "The registration could not be completed. Please try again later."; the form and the entered values stay; nothing from the response body is shown.

# Email contract (backend → SMTP)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: spec section 8, US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07 · Agent: writes

Both messages are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist (spec section 5). A send failure is logged with the registration id only and does not change the API answer (OQ-03).

## Common rules

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| From | `registration.mail.from` (default `registration@konferenca.si`) |
| Recipients | exactly one `To` address per message, built from the address alone (no display name); no `Cc`, no `Bcc` |
| Subject | fixed text plus the configured conference name; never contains user input |
| Body | `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`; no HTML part; user input appears only here, as literal text |
| Headers | no header contains user input (SR-05) |

## Participant confirmation (US-006)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| To | the participant's email (trimmed, validated) |
| Subject | `Registration confirmed: <conference name>` |
| Body | see template |

```
Dear <firstName> <lastName>,

thank you for registering for <conference name>. Your registration has been received.

Registration type: <External participant | Student>
Selected options:
- <option name> (<Workshop | Event | Meal | Other activity>)
...                       (or the single line "- none")

Registration ID: <id>
```

## Organizer notification (US-007)

One message per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (comma separated, blanks ignored).

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| To | one organizer address |
| Subject | `New registration: <conference name>` |
| Structure | `multipart/mixed`: the text body, then one attachment |
| Attachment | file name `registration-<id>.json`, content type `application/json`, content byte-for-byte equal to the stored JSON copy `<id>.json` (AC-007-02) |
| Body | see template; only registration data (SR-07) |

```
A new registration was received for <conference name>.

Registration ID: <id>
Registered at: <registeredAt, ISO-8601 UTC>
Type: <EXTERNAL | STUDENT>
First name: <firstName>
Last name: <lastName>
Email: <email>
Organization / institution: <organization>      (EXTERNAL)
Study institution: <studyInstitution>           (STUDENT)
Study programme: <studyProgramme>               (STUDENT)
Student ID: <studentId>                         (STUDENT)
Options:
- <option name> (<category label>)              (or "- none")
Consents:
- <consent id>: given <givenAt>

The raw registration is attached as JSON.
```

# Runtime image only: the jar is built on the host with ./mvnw package (tech-stack.md lists the JRE image).
FROM eclipse-temurin:21.0.10_7-jre-alpine

 && mkdir -p /app /data/json-copies \
 && chown app:app /data/json-copies
WORKDIR /app

WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json .npmrc ./
RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
COPY index.html tsconfig.json vite.config.ts vitest.config.ts playwright.config.ts ./
COPY src ./src
COPY tests ./tests
COPY e2e ./e2e
RUN npm run build

FROM nginx:1.30.5-alpine
COPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
COPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
RUN mkdir -p /tmp/nginx && chown -R nginx:nginx /tmp/nginx /usr/share/nginx/html
USER nginx
EXPOSE 8080
EOF
cat > frontend/.dockerignore <<'EOF'
node_modules
dist
coverage
reports
.stryker-tmp
playwright-report
test-results
EOF
cat > frontend/nginx.conf <<'EOF'
# Serves the built frontend and proxies /api to the backend (AR-01). Runs as the nginx user (SB-11).
worker_processes auto;
pid /tmp/nginx/nginx.pid;
error_log /dev/stderr warn;

events {
  worker_connections 1024;
}

http {
  include /etc/nginx/mime.types;
  default_type application/octet-stream;
  server_tokens off;
  access_log /dev/stdout;
  sendfile on;

  client_body_temp_path /tmp/nginx/client_body;
  proxy_temp_path /tmp/nginx/proxy;
  fastcgi_temp_path /tmp/nginx/fastcgi;
  uwsgi_temp_path /tmp/nginx/uwsgi;
  scgi_temp_path /tmp/nginx/scgi;

  server {
    listen 8080;
    server_name _;
    root /usr/share/nginx/html;

    # SB-10: security headers; reCAPTCHA hosts are the only third-party sources.
    add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'" always;
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
    add_header X-Frame-Options "DENY" always;
    add_header Referrer-Policy "no-referrer" always;

    location /api/ {
      client_max_body_size 16k;
      proxy_pass http://backend:8080;
      # SR-08: never forward the client's Host header; the client address replaces any forwarded chain.
      proxy_set_header Host backend;
      proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
      proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
      proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host "";
    }

    location / {
      try_files $uri /index.html;
    }
  }
}
EOF
cat > docker-compose.yml <<'EOF'
# Local stack (environments.md, "local"): every port on 127.0.0.1 only, plain HTTP.
# Secrets come from the repository-root .env; build the backend jar first (./mvnw package).
name: konferenca-registration

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16.15-alpine
    env_file:
      - path: ../.env
        required: true
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: registration
      POSTGRES_USER: registration
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U registration -d registration"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

  mailpit:
    image: axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8025:8025"
      - "127.0.0.1:1025:1025"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "/mailpit", "readyz"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

  backend:
    build: ./backend
    env_file:
      - path: ../.env
        required: true
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/registration
      DATABASE_USER: registration
      SMTP_HOST: mailpit
      SMTP_PORT: "1025"
      SMTP_STARTTLS: "false"
      SMTP_USERNAME: ""
      SMTP_PASSWORD: ""
      NVD_API_KEY: ""
      REGISTRATION_CONFERENCE_NAME: "Konferenca 2026"
      REGISTRATION_JSON_COPY_DIR: /data/json-copies
      RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE: "true"
      ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY: "false"
    volumes:
      - jsoncopies:/data/json-copies
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      mailpit:
        condition: service_started
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health/readiness"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      start_period: 60s
      retries: 10

  frontend:
    build: ./frontend
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8081:8080"
    depends_on:
      backend:
        condition: service_started
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10

volumes:
  pgdata:
  jsoncopies:
EOF
docker compose config --quiet 2>&1 | head -5; echo config=$?

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

#!/bin/sh
# Runtime demonstration of the local stack (phase 6). Never prints secret values.
cd "E:/13 - Lab Projects/01_Runs/_____SECOND______ROUND_____/04_kyuhi_single-agent_sdd_v006/02_output" || exit 1
U="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_USERNAME=//p' ../.env | tr -d '\r')"
P="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_PASSWORD=//p' ../.env | tr -d '\r')"
psql() { docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U registration -d registration -At -c "$1"; }
step() { echo; echo "### $*"; }

step "state before recreation"
docker compose ps --format '{{.Service}} {{.State}} {{.Health}}'
BEFORE_ROWS=$(psql "SELECT count(*) FROM registration")
BEFORE_FILES=$(docker compose exec -T backend sh -c 'ls /data/json-copies | wc -l' | tr -d '\r ')
echo "registrations=$BEFORE_ROWS json_copies=$BEFORE_FILES"

step "NFR-02: docker compose down (containers removed, volumes kept) then up --wait"
docker compose down 2>&1 | tail -2
docker compose up -d --wait 2>&1 | tail -2
docker compose ps --format '{{.Service}} {{.State}} {{.Health}}'
AFTER_ROWS=$(psql "SELECT count(*) FROM registration")
AFTER_FILES=$(docker compose exec -T backend sh -c 'ls /data/json-copies | wc -l' | tr -d '\r ')
echo "registrations=$AFTER_ROWS json_copies=$AFTER_FILES (before: $BEFORE_ROWS / $BEFORE_FILES)"

step "NFR-04: health and readiness"
for p in /actuator/health /actuator/health/liveness /actuator/health/readiness /actuator/env /actuator/beans; do
  echo "$p -> $(curl -s -o /tmp/h.txt -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8080$p) $(head -c 80 /tmp/h.txt)"
done

step "DoD-P01: one external and one student registration through the frontend proxy"
for kind in EXTERNAL STUDENT; do
  if [ $kind = EXTERNAL ]; then extra='"organization":"Demo Org","optionIds":["ws-security","ev-dinner"]'; else extra='"studyInstitution":"Univerza v Mariboru","studyProgramme":"Računalništvo","studentId":"63219999","optionIds":["ws-testing","meal-lunch-1"]'; fi
  body="{\"type\":\"$kind\",\"firstName\":\"Demo\",\"lastName\":\"Šuštar $kind\",\"email\":\"demo-$kind-$$@example.com\",$extra,\"consents\":[\"privacy\"],\"recaptchaToken\":\"test-mode-token\"}"
  curl -s -o /tmp/r.txt -w "%{http_code} " -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary "$body" http://127.0.0.1:8081/api/registrations; cat /tmp/r.txt; echo

# Conference registration

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-06 · Agent: writes

## Overview

Online registration for a conference. External participants and students fill in a form, choose workshops, events, meals and other activities, and confirm the mandatory consent. Each accepted registration is stored in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy, the participant gets a confirmation email and every organizer gets a notification with the JSON copy attached. Organizers download all registrations as an Excel workbook. The form is protected by Google reCAPTCHA v2.

## Components

| Component | What it is | README |
|---|---|---|
| backend | Spring Boot REST API under `/api` (Java 21) | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) |
| frontend | React single page built with Vite, served by nginx, which also proxies `/api` | [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) |

The local stack (`docker-compose.yml`) runs both components with PostgreSQL and Mailpit.

## Quick start (local stack)

Prerequisites: Docker Engine with Compose, JDK 21, Node.js 24 (versions in `01_input/01_project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`).

# Backend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

Spring Boot REST API (root package `si.konferenca.registration`): form configuration, registrations, Excel export, emails, JSON copies. Architecture and contracts: `../docs/02_specification.md`, `../docs/02_contracts/`.

## Prerequisites

- JDK 21 (Temurin); Maven comes with the wrapper (`./mvnw`, Maven 3.9.9).
- Docker for the tests (Testcontainers starts PostgreSQL and Mailpit) and for the container image.

## Configuration

Every setting is an environment variable (spec section 13); `src/main/resources/application.properties` maps each one. Secrets come from `.env` (template `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example`), never from code.

| Variable | Secret | Default (local/test only) |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_USER` | no | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/registration`, `registration` |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | yes | none |
| `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_STARTTLS` | no | `localhost`, `1025`, `false` |
| `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | yes | empty |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | yes | none |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | no | `true` (set `false` only for local plain HTTP) |
| `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | no | `false` (`true` locally and in tests) |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | yes | empty |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | no | Google siteverify |
| `REGISTRATION_CONFERENCE_NAME`, `REGISTRATION_MAIL_FROM` | no | `Conference`, `registration@konferenca.si` |
| `REGISTRATION_CONFERENCE_CONFIG` | no | `classpath:conference.json` (options and consents, schema `../docs/02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`) |
| `REGISTRATION_JSON_COPY_DIR` | no | `./data/json-copies` |
| `REGISTRATION_RATE_LIMIT_FORM_CONFIG`, `_REGISTRATIONS`, `_EXPORT`, `REGISTRATION_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | no | `120`, `20`, `10` per minute, `16384` |
| `REGISTRATION_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | no | empty (local development only) |

Production: `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod` removes the local defaults and refuses to start with reCAPTCHA test mode on, empty reCAPTCHA keys or `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false`.

## Commands (ES-05)

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| Build | `./mvnw -B package -DskipTests` (jar in `target/`) |
| Test | `./mvnw -B test` (unit, acceptance with Testcontainers, architecture; needs Docker) |
| Check | `./mvnw -B spotless:check compile pmd:check pmd:cpd-check spotbugs:check` |
| Run | `./mvnw spring-boot:run` with the variables above exported (or `docker compose up` in `..`) |
| Format | `./mvnw spotless:apply` |
| Coverage | `./mvnw -B test jacoco:report` (report in `target/site/jacoco`) |
| Mutation | `./mvnw -B test-compile org.pitest:pitest-maven:mutationCoverage` (report in `target/pit-reports`) |
| Dependency scan | `NVD_API_KEY=... ./mvnw org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:check` |

Health: `GET /actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness`.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| Start fails with "Could not resolve placeholder 'ORGANIZER_EMAILS'" (or another secret) | the variable is not set; secrets have no default |
| Start fails with "Invalid conference configuration: …" | the options file violates its schema; the message names the option and the rule |
| "Refusing to start in production: …" | the `prod` profile found test mode on, empty reCAPTCHA keys or HTTPS-only off |
| Tests fail with Docker or Testcontainers errors | start Docker; the tests start `postgres:16.15-alpine` and `axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1` |
| Export answers 403 "HTTPS is required." | plain HTTP from a non-local client; use HTTPS through the proxy or, locally only, `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false` |
| Registrations answer 429 | the per-client rate limit; wait for the `Retry-After` seconds or raise the limit variables |

# Frontend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

React single page (Vite) with the registration form, client-side validation, backend field errors next to the fields, and the confirmation. It talks to the backend only through `/api` (AR-01). UI contract: `../docs/02_contracts/ui.md`.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24 with npm 11 (exact versions in `tech-stack.md`); install dependencies with `npm ci`.
- For end-to-end tests: the local stack (`docker compose up` in `..`) and Playwright's Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` once).

## Configuration

The frontend has no secrets and no build-time settings (AR-07). The conference name, options, consents, the reCAPTCHA site key and the test-mode flag come from `GET /api/form-config` at runtime. In development, Vite proxies `/api` to `http://127.0.0.1:8080`; in the container, nginx (`nginx.conf`) proxies `/api/` to `http://backend:8080` and sets the security headers.

End-to-end tests read `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` and `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` from the environment or from the repository-root `.env`; `E2E_BASE_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8081`) and `E2E_MAILPIT_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8025`) may be overridden.

## Commands (ES-05)

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| Install | `npm ci` |
| Build | `npm run build` (type check, then static files in `dist/`) |
| Test | `npm test` (unit and acceptance tests, Vitest) |
| Check | `npm run check` (Prettier, ESLint, `tsc --noEmit`) |
| Run | `npm run dev` (http://127.0.0.1:5173, backend on 8080) or the `frontend` service of `docker compose` |
| End-to-end | `npm run e2e` (Playwright against the running local stack) |
| Coverage | `npm run coverage` |
| Mutation | `npm run mutation` (Stryker, report in `reports/mutation`) |
| Duplication | `npm run duplication` (jscpd) |
| Dependency scan | `npm audit` |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| Page shows "The registration form is currently unavailable." | `/api/form-config` failed: start the backend (dev server) or check `docker compose ps` |
| E2E tests fail with `ORGANIZER_USERNAME is not set` | export the organizer login or create the repository-root `.env` |
| E2E tests fail on `docker compose exec` | the stack is not running; start it in `..` |
| Playwright cannot find a browser | run `npx playwright install chromium` |

# Release notes

> Written in: phase 7 · Agent: writes

Version 1.0.0 of the conference registration (backend and frontend).

## Delivered

- Registration forms for external participants and students with the fixed fields of BR-01, active options grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and the mandatory `privacy` consent (US-001, US-002, OQ-01, OQ-02).
- Options and consents from a JSON configuration file; an invalid file stops the backend (US-003, AR-04).
- Confirmation in the page only after acceptance; field errors next to the fields; general error without details (US-004).
- Storage in PostgreSQL (Flyway migration V1) plus a raw JSON copy per registration, written in one unit (US-005, AR-05).
- Participant confirmation email and one organizer notification per address with the JSON copy attached (US-006, US-007); email failures keep the registration (OQ-03).
- Excel export for the organizer over HTTP Basic, HTTPS-only for non-local clients (US-008, SR-06).
- reCAPTCHA v2 verified on the backend; test mode only by configuration; production refuses unsafe settings (SR-01, SR-02).
- Rate limits, 16 KiB body limit, security headers, non-root containers, health and readiness endpoints (SR-03, SB-10, SB-11, NFR-04).
- Quality: 290 automated tests green (backend 216, frontend 69, end-to-end 5); line coverage 99.32 % / 100 %, mutation score 95.72 % / 94.83 % (backend / frontend).

## Known limitations

- Retention (OQ-06): registrations and JSON copies are never deleted automatically. **The operator must delete the database rows (`registration`, cascading to options and consents) and the files in the JSON copy volume no later than 12 months after the conference.**
- Rate limits are kept in memory per backend instance; with several instances each counts separately, and a restart resets them.
- The client address used for rate limits and the HTTPS-only rule comes from `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Forwarded-Proto` only when the proxy is a trusted internal address (Tomcat defaults: 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 127/8). If the production proxy has another address, set `server.tomcat.remoteip.internal-proxies` accordingly.
- With an unreachable database the production start fails on the database before the safety check runs (F-07); with the database reachable, unsafe settings are refused.
- Emails are sent synchronously after storage (D-11); a slow SMTP server delays the answer by up to the 5-second timeouts.
- The backend image needs the jar built on the host first (`./mvnw package`), because only the JRE image is in the tech stack.
- Accepted findings: Semgrep `npm-missing-minimum-release-age` (F-02, needs npm ≥ 11.10), npm audit moderate advisories in dev-only Stryker dependencies (F-05).

## Must be tested manually by a human

| What | How |
|---|---|
| Google reCAPTCHA v2 with production keys | set `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=false`; submit one real registration in a browser (the widget appears and the registration is accepted), and one with an expired token (rejected) |
| Email delivery through the real SMTP server | set `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` (STARTTLS on in `prod`); register with a real mailbox; check the confirmation and the organizer notification with its JSON attachment, including Slovenian characters |
| TLS and the reverse proxy | external nginx with Let's Encrypt: HTTP redirects to HTTPS, `/` serves the frontend, `/api` reaches the backend; the proxy sets `Host` itself and overwrites `X-Forwarded-For` (SR-08) and sets `X-Forwarded-Proto https` |
| HTTPS-only export | with valid credentials, the export over HTTPS works and a plain-HTTP request from another machine is refused (403) |
| Production start | start with `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod`; confirm it refuses with test mode on and starts with the real keys |
| Backup and retention | the `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` volumes are in the backup; deletion after 12 months as above |

## Decisions pending review

| Decision | Chosen behaviour |
|---|---|
| D-08 | length limits (100 / 254 / 200 / 50 characters, 100 options), fields of the other type and unknown properties rejected, email pattern |
| D-09 | 403 for the HTTPS-only refusal, 500 for storage failures |
| D-10 | rate limits 120 / 20 / 10 per client and minute, 16 KiB body limit |
| D-11 | emails sent synchronously, plain text, one message per organizer address |

All other decisions (D-01 … D-07, D-12 … D-14) are resolved; see `decisions-log.md`.

# Conference registration

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-06 · Agent: writes

## Overview

Online registration for a conference. External participants and students fill in a form, choose workshops, events, meals and other activities, and confirm the mandatory consent. Each accepted registration is stored in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy, the participant gets a confirmation email and every organizer gets a notification with the JSON copy attached. Organizers download all registrations as an Excel workbook. The form is protected by Google reCAPTCHA v2.

## Components

| Component | What it is | README |
|---|---|---|
| backend | Spring Boot REST API under `/api` (Java 21) | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) |
| frontend | React single page built with Vite, served by nginx, which also proxies `/api` | [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) |

The local stack (`docker-compose.yml`) runs both components with PostgreSQL and Mailpit.

## Quick start (local stack)

Prerequisites: Docker Engine with Compose, JDK 21, Node.js 24 (versions in `01_input/01_project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`).

1. Create `.env` in the repository root (one level above this folder) from `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` and fill `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (16+ random characters) and `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`. reCAPTCHA keys are not needed locally (test mode).
2. Build the backend jar (the image copies it):
   ```bash
   cd backend && ./mvnw -B package -DskipTests && cd ..
   ```
3. Start everything:
   ```bash
   docker compose up -d --build --wait
   ```
4. Open http://127.0.0.1:8081 (form; reCAPTCHA is the test-mode checkbox), http://127.0.0.1:8025 (Mailpit: every email), and download the export with the organizer login from `.env`:
   ```bash
   curl -u "$ORGANIZER_USERNAME:$ORGANIZER_PASSWORD" -o registrations.xlsx http://127.0.0.1:8081/api/organizer/registrations.xlsx
   ```
5. Stop with `docker compose down` (data stays on the `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` volumes; `docker compose down -v` deletes it).

End-to-end tests run against this stack: `cd frontend && npm run e2e`.
